228:## Changes from the blueprint
229-
230-- **Success after a cancel or a move comes from `list_bookings`:** the blueprint says only `get_booking_status` can report success, but that tool knows only `book` attempts, and the provider contract cannot change.
231-- **A move builds its slot from the user's words:** `propose_reschedule` takes a day in the user's words and a time. The blueprint passes a slot, which would make the model work out a date. It saves nothing, so an errand in progress keeps its dates.
232-- **A change card lasts 10 minutes:** the provider's `cancel` and `reschedule` take no hold, so the card has its own expiry. An expired card closes, and an old yes changes nothing.

    if (raw) return JSON.parse(raw) as T;
  } catch {
    // Blocked or corrupt storage just means starting empty.
  }
  return fallback;
}

function write(key: string, value: unknown): void {

    localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value));
  } catch {
    // The chat still works for this page load.
  }
}

```
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";

import { ApiError } from "../../lib/api";
import { USER_ID } from "../../lib/user";
import { fetchMemories } from "./api";
import type { MemoryItem } from "./types";

export function memoryErrorText(error: unknown): string {
  return error instanceof ApiError ? error.message : "Could not reach the server.";
}

export function useMemories(refreshKey: string) {
  const [memories, setMemories] = useState<MemoryItem[] | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setMemories(await fetchMemories(USER_ID));
      setError(null);
    } catch (reason) {
      setError(memoryErrorText(reason));
    }
  }, []);

  // A chat turn can add or forget a memory, so read again after each one.
  useEffect(() => {
    void load();
  }, [load, refreshKey]);

  return { memories, error, setError, load };
}
```

**Claude:**

The redesign is done and running at `http://localhost:3000`. I couldn't test it with a real Gemini reply, because the daily quota ran out and the app reports about 17 hours until it resets.

**What changed**
- **Design:** It's light mode only, with warm neutrals, one clay accent, and serif text for replies and headings, like the Claude app. It has its own house logo, not Claude's.
- **Previous chats:** A sidebar has New chat and Recents. Opening an old chat brings back its messages, and new messages continue in the same session.
- **Trace and Memory:** Each is now a top-bar button that opens a side panel. Both start closed, and only one shows at a time. "View trace" under a reply also opens the Trace panel.
- **Trace panel:** Steps are now an expandable timeline, and problems and suspicious text start open.
- **Memory panel:** The top-bar button shows a count, which turns amber if a memory needs your answer. Those memories are listed first in the panel.
- **Service status:** The old status bar is now a top-bar menu saying "All services up", or naming the service that is down. "Run test job" moved into this menu.
- **Chat:** The empty screen has a centred greeting, the message box grows as you type, and the approval cards are redesigned. Replies now render Markdown, including tables.
- **Phone layout:** The sidebar becomes a drawer and panels fill the screen.

**Libraries**
- **Added:** `lucide-react` for icons, and `react-markdown` with `remark-gfm` and `remark-breaks` for replies.
- **Left out:** Tailwind and Radix felt like overkill, so the shared components are in [ui.tsx](web/src/components/ui.tsx) and the styling is plain CSS in [styles.css](web/src/styles.css).
- **Links and images:** The model's text can't create a link or load an image, because it reads provider reviews that can contain prompt injections.

**Testing**
- **UI tests:** All 60 pass, 12 of them new. I also changed the existing tests to match the new layout.
- **Browser check:** I ran the rebuilt container in headless Chromium, with no browser errors and no sideways scroll at 390 px or 1000 px.
- **Not covered:** That run used made-up chat, trace and approval responses, so please send a real message once the quota resets. I also didn't run `make check` or the integration tests, because no server code changed.

**Good to know**
- **Chat history stays in the browser:** The server has no history endpoint, so it's stored in `localStorage`, up to 50 chats. Another browser or a cleared cache won't show them. Sharing history across browsers would need a new server endpoint.

- **Leftover files:** Test screenshots remain in the session scratchpad because a safety check blocked my cleanup; they're safe to ignore.

I updated `BUILD_LOG.md` with these changes and the testing gap.

# Real bugs hit while building

Candidates for the "three real bugs" deliverable. Each one really happened, and each has a test that guards it.

## 1. A killed worker's job never came back on a quiet queue

- **What broke:** After `kill -9` on a worker mid-job, the job stayed undelivered. With a 5 s idle timeout it had still not returned after 40 s.
- **Why:** In `taskiq-redis`, the reclaim step comes after `if not fetched: continue`. So it only runs when a new job arrives. On a quiet queue, it never runs.
- **Fix:** Recovery no longer depends on the broker. Jobs have leases in PostgreSQL, and a sweep every 15 s requeues expired ones.
- **Regression test:** `test_killed_worker_on_a_quiet_queue_recovers_through_the_sweep` in `server/tests/integration/test_worker_recovery.py`.

cd /Users/aviroop/Documents/code/orange-assignment; python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p='BUGS.md'
s=open(p).read()
heads=list(re.finditer(r'^## (\d+)\. .*$', s, re.M))
n=int(heads[-1].group(1))+1
later=re.search(r'^#{1,2} (?!\d+\.)', s[heads[-1].end():], re.M)
at=heads[-1].end()+later.start() if later else len(s)
entry=f'''## {n}. A new state move broke a safety rule, and the docs still claimed it

- **What broke:** The proactive work made `INTAKE` to `DONE` legal, so a blank errand can give way. Two state machine tests failed, and the N6 row in the build log still said no other path reaches `DONE`. Only GitHub CI caught it, because that change ran only the test files it touched.
- **Why:** The rule was written as "only VERIFYING reaches DONE". What it must protect is narrower: nothing that executed can reach `DONE` without a status check.
- **Fix:** The move stays, because the unique index on active errands needs it. `reopen_in` allows it only for a blank errand. The test now walks every path out of `EXECUTING`, and the N6 row says what is true.
- **Regression test:** `test_nothing_that_executed_reaches_done_without_verifying` in `server/tests/unit/test_workflow.py`.

'''
s=s[:at].rstrip('\n')+'\n\n'+entry+s[at:] if later else s.rstrip('\n')+'\n\n'+entry.rstrip('\n')+'\n'
open(p,'w').write(s)

**Claude:**

Memory stores facts about the user, and the ContextAssembler decides what the model sees on each call. The transcript stays uncommitted.

## The problem it solves
Today ADK sends the full chat history on every model call. That causes two problems:
- **Cost grows with the chat:** a single correction turn after two searches already used 12,821 input tokens across 3 calls.
- **Forgetting can't work:** ADK's history is append-only. If you say "forget my address", the memory row can be removed, but the address is still in the old messages the model receives.

## What the ContextAssembler is
It's one piece of code that runs in `before_model_callback`, just before every model call. It throws away what ADK prepared and builds the request itself. That includes calls in the middle of a run, such as after a tool returns.

The assembler builds each request in five steps:
1. **Gather:** it collects the pieces listed in the table below.
2. **Filter:** SQL keeps only memories that are active, not superseded, and either explicit or confirmed by the user. An unconfirmed fact never reaches the ranking step.
3. **Rank:** a fixed score on service and scope puts the relevant memories first. For an AC request, "my AC is a Daikin" beats "I prefer a female plumber". There are no embeddings, so evals give the same result offline.
4. **Trim:** it cuts down to 8,000 estimated tokens, using a cautious chars / 3 estimate.
5. **Log:** it writes the full request and the token count per piece to `context_log` before the call. If that write fails, the model call doesn't run.

| Piece | Source | When over budget |
|---|---|---|
| System prompt and tool declarations | Code | Always kept, and counted |
| Workflow state and booking news | `errand` database | Kept |
| Current request and current tool calls | This run | Kept, but large tool results shrink first |
| Older turns | `turn_view` | Cut first |
| Summary of the older chat | Stored summary | Cut second |
| Memories | `memories` table | Cut last, lowest rank first |

## How it connects to memory
- **`turn_view`:** this is our own copy of the chat, which we can edit. The assembler reads this, not ADK's log.
- **Forgetting:** this marks the memory as forgotten, removes the text from `turn_view`, rebuilds the summary and deletes the old ADK session. Without the assembler, none of this would keep the fact from the model.
- **Worker news:** the worker can't write to ADK sessions, so a proactive cancellation notice enters through the assembler on the next turn.
- **Trimming is safe for the errand:** the area, budget and dates live on the workflow row, so cutting old chat doesn't lose them. The assembler takes over the small version of this that `instruction()` does today in [runtime.py:44](server/app/domains/agent/runtime.py:44).

## What it doesn't do
It adds no booking safety. The approval and saga rules stay exactly as they are, and it only controls what the model knows.

## How we prove it
- **E26:** 60 memories and a long chat stay within budget on every call, and only relevant facts are sent.
- **E22 and I4:** seeded marker strings are searched for in every logged context. A forgotten, superseded or unconfirmed one must never appear.
- **I5:** every logged context is within the budget.

## One gap to settle
The blueprint needs a summary and says to rebuild it on forget, but it doesn't say who writes it.
- **Code-built (my pick):** this means a short summary made from structured facts such as past errands and outcomes. It's repeatable offline, costs no model call, and can't bring back forgotten text unless that text is in the source rows.
- **Model-written:** this would read better, but it uses free-tier calls and makes evals less repeatable. It could also carry forgotten text forward in reworded form, which a marker search might miss.

cat > core/redaction.py <<'EOF'
"""Removes a fact's text from anything we stored. Forgetting must reach every copy."""

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any

REMOVED = "[removed]"


def compile_patterns(values: Iterable[str]) -> re.Pattern[str] | None:
    """Longest first, so a whole phrase goes before a part of it. Whole words only."""
    parts = sorted({value.strip() for value in values if value.strip()}, key=len, reverse=True)
    if not parts:
        return None
    escaped = (r"\s+".join(re.escape(word) for word in part.split()) for part in parts)
    return re.compile(rf"(?<!\w)(?:{'|'.join(escaped)})(?!\w)", re.IGNORECASE)


def scrub_text(text: str, pattern: re.Pattern[str] | None) -> str:
    return pattern.sub(REMOVED, text) if pattern else text


def scrub_value(value: Any, pattern: re.Pattern[str] | None) -> Any:
    """Every string inside a JSON-like value. Keys and other types stay as they are."""
    if pattern is None:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return pattern.sub(REMOVED, value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: scrub_value(item, pattern) for key, item in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [scrub_value(item, pattern) for item in value]
    return value
EOF

/** The only fake in UI tests: the HTTP boundary. Everything above it is the real app. */
type Handler = (body: unknown) => { status?: number; json: unknown } | Promise<never>;

export function fakeApi(routes: Record<string, Handler>) {
  const calls: { key: string; body: unknown }[] = [];
  const fetchMock = vi.fn(async (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const key = `${init?.method ?? "GET"} ${String(input)}`;
    const body = init?.body ? JSON.parse(String(init.body)) : undefined;
    calls.push({ key, body });
    const handler = routes[key];
    if (!handler) {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ detail: "not found" }), { status: 404 });
    }
    const result = await handler(body);
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(result.json), { status: result.status ?? 200 });
  });
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", fetchMock);
  return calls;
}

**Claude:**

Memory and the ContextAssembler are built and running on your local stack at `http://localhost:3000`. Nothing is committed: the work is on branch `memory-context`, and the refreshed transcript is still uncommitted too.

## What you can try
- **Save a fact:** say "I live in Indiranagar, remember that." It appears on the new Memory panel, and a new chat uses it without asking.
- **Correct or forget a fact:** do it in chat or on the panel, and the old value stops reaching the model.
- **See the seeded data:** open `http://localhost:3000/?user=seed-user` to see 40 trusted facts and 8 unconfirmed ones.
- **See what was sent:** each model call now shows a "Context built" row in the trace.

## What the live Gemini run showed
- **Full flow:** it saved a fact, used it in a new chat, corrected it, then forgot it.
- **Forgetting:** afterwards neither area name was in `turn_view`, `context_log`, the errand, runs, trace events or ADK rows.
- **Budget:** the seeded user (60 memories, 240 chat messages) used an estimated 7,979 and 7,991 of 8,000 tokens. Gemini's real counts were 6,240 and 6,647.
- **Filtering:** unconfirmed, superseded and forgotten markers appeared in no logged context.

## Testing
- **What ran:**
    - the server unit test files this change touches, including the new `test_memory.py`
    - 43 UI tests
    - lint, types and import rules
    - `alembic check` on Postgres, which found no drift from the models
    - a headless Chromium layout check at three widths
- **What didn't run:** the full suite and integration tests, as you asked. CI runs them on the PR, so a failure could still show up there.
- **No integration test yet:** this feature has none of its own, so on Postgres it has only the live run and `alembic check` behind it.
- **Deliberate-break audit:** still on hold, so these tests haven't been proven to catch a break.

## Limits you may notice
- **Asking "what do you remember?" sends every trusted fact:** that includes facts about other services, for that turn. This happened in the seeded live run. It's the one known exception to "only relevant facts", so tell me if you'd rather have it ranked too.
- **Forgetting matches exact text:** if the model reworded a fact, such as "Indira Nagar" for "Indiranagar", the reworded copy stays in the stored chat.
- **Duplicate keys:** the model chooses each fact's key, so one fact could end up under two keys. Both would show on the panel.
- **Past bookings:** "same as last time" still relies on the prompt, so F8 stays Partial and E20 is not started.

## Build log
- **Status:** functional requirements are now 12 done, 1 partial and 1 not started. Non-functional are 11 done and 9 partial.
- **Blueprint changes:** I logged them, including that the summary is now built by code on each read and is not stored.
- **Bugs:** I added one to `BUGS.md`: a typed yes or no never reached the model's history. It has a regression test.
- **CI note:** the out-of-date note is fixed.

Proactive cancellation, SSE and JSONL traces are next, when you say.

- **Why the location was missed:** the model made only one save call, for the schedule. The prompt doesn't tell it to save each fact separately.

**Claude:**

Both issues are fixed and running on your local stack. Your exact message now saves both facts without you saying "remember", and with no question.

## What changed
- **Automatic saving:** the agent now watches every message for lasting facts and saves them straight away. If a message only gives facts, it saves them and then asks what you need.
- **One save per fact:** "I live in Indiranagar and go to office..." now makes two saves, one for `area` and one for `work_schedule`.
- **Word endings:** "goes to office" now counts as your statement, as we discussed.
- **Shown in the chat:** a saved fact appears under the reply as "Remembered area: Indiranagar".
- **Asked in the chat:** if your words don't clearly state a fact, a "Remember this?" card appears with Remember and Don't remember buttons. You can also type "yes", "remember that" or "no".

## Live Gemini results

| Message | What happened |
|---|---|
| Your exact message | Saved both facts, no question |
| "I prefer Hindi speaking technicians and nothing before 10 am" | Saved the language. Asked about the time, because the model wrote "not before 10 am" |
| A fact plus a request for an electrician | Saved the fact, and the search still ran |
| "Plumber in Koramangala tomorrow, budget 1000" | Saved nothing, which is right for a one-off errand |
| A fact, then "remember that" | Saved it once, and the agent said it already had it |

## Rules I chose
- **Save first, ask only when unsure:** a fact you clearly stated is saved without asking, because the "Remembered" line shows it and you can correct or forget it. Tell me if you'd rather be asked every time.
- **A question lasts one message:** if you move on, the card closes and the fact waits on the Memory panel. A later "yes" to something else can't confirm it.
- **Booking cards come first:** if a booking card is open, "yes" answers that card.

## Another bug I found
Saying no to a guess would also have forgotten the real fact under the same key. It now drops only the guess. This and your report are in `BUGS.md` with regression tests.

## Limits
- **Spotting a fact is still the model's judgement:** only the prompt asks for it, so it can miss a fact or save a one-off detail. Five live chats don't show how often that happens.
- **The check matches words, not meaning:** "I don't like Rahul" could pass as "likes Rahul". You would see it in the chat and could correct it.
- **More Gemini calls:** a turn that saves a fact usually needs one extra model call, which counts against the free-tier limit of 15 a minute.

**Claude:**

The date problem is fixed: replaying your exact chat on live Gemini now gets to a real date and a search. It's running on your local stack.

## Why it kept asking
The model wasn't the main problem. My date code refused its answers each time:

| You said | The model sent | What went wrong |
|---|---|---|
| "next week sometime" | "next week sometime" | The reader didn't know "sometime" |
| "lets do thur" | "Thursday next week" | This was correct, but you wrote "thur", and my check compares whole words, so "Thursday" counted as something you never said |
| "cant you find out the date?" | "Thursday next week" | Same refusal |

Each refusal told the model to ask you for a date, so it kept asking.

## What I fixed
- **Short words:** "thur" and "Thursday", "nov" and "November", "14th" and "14", and "tmrw" and "tomorrow" now count as the same word.
- **Loose words:** "sometime", "anytime" and "whenever" are ignored next to a real date. On its own, "sometime" still gets a question.
- **Narrowing a range:** after "next week", a bare "thur" now means next week's Thursday. The first replay gave this Thursday (05/11), because the model dropped "next week" again, so this rule is in code, not the prompt. "This Thursday" still means this Thursday.
- **No more asking for a calendar date:** the refusals and the prompt now say the tool works the date out.
- **A related bug:** "Tuesday or Thursday next week" used to start from this Tuesday. The week now applies to both days.

## The replay

| You said | Result |
|---|---|
| "next week sometime" | 09/11/2026 to 15/11/2026, and it searched |
| "anyday im not working" | It used your saved schedule and suggested Tuesday, Thursday or the weekend |
| "lets do thur" | Thursday 12/11/2026, and it searched |

## Still open
- **Word check is loose:** it only asks that each word appeared somewhere in the chat. "Sat" in "I sat at home" counts as Saturday, and "Mon" in your work schedule counts as Monday. The exact date is always shown, and a booking still needs your confirmation on the card.
- **"Tuesday or Thursday" also covers Wednesday:** it searches the whole range between the two days, so Wednesday slots can appear.
- **Raw slot format:** one live reply listed a slot as `2026-11-12T09:00:00+...`, not as a readable time. I haven't changed this. It's a small display fix if you want it in this PR.

This is the second date bug with the same cause as "Wednesday next week": my tests used clean words, and you type short ones. The new tests use your actual messages, and it's logged as bug 13 in `BUGS.md`.

I only ran `test_dates.py` and `test_workflow.py`, plus lint and types. Nothing is committed: it's still on `memory-context`, and the transcript stays uncommitted too.

**Claude:**

**Your tool results were correct. The model made up the Tuesday slots, and my code set it up to do that.** No wrong booking was possible: code refused all three attempts, and no card ever appeared. I haven't changed any code yet.

## What the provider really has

I queried the mock provider directly, and it matches what we stored from the search.

| Provider | Total slots next week | Tuesday 10/11 |
|---|---|---|
| Quick AC Care | 34 | **None** |
| Trusted AC Care | 34 | 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 |
| City AC Care | 36 | 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 |

## What the model said, turn by turn

| You said | Tool call | Model said | True? |
|---|---|---|---|
| "lets go with quick" | `get_provider`, which has no slots | Monday 10:00 or 11:00 | Yes |
| "what do you suggest" | None | Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 | **No, made up** |
| "lets do tue" | `propose_booking` Tue 10:00, **refused** | No Tuesday slots | Yes, it had this right |
| "you just said..." | None | Apologised, then listed six Tuesday slots, and said "you work on Tuesdays" | **No, on both.** Your schedule is saved as Mon, Wed, Fri |
| "lets do 12" | `propose_booking` Tue 12:00, **refused** | Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 | **No, made up** |
| "lets do 11?" | `propose_booking` Tue 11:00, **refused** | Tuesday 10:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 | **No, made up** |

## Why it happened

1. **The model can't see most of the slots (my code).** The search result shows only the first 6 of 34 slots, and later turns show the first 8 plus "(26 more)". For Quick AC Care that means Monday and part of Wednesday. No tool can read the rest, so it couldn't answer a question about Tuesday. The 6-slot cap is older, but my new assembler kept the same kind of cut, with 8.
2. **It probably mixed up providers.** The made-up times match the other two providers' Tuesday slots, which sit on the lines right next to Quick's in what it was sent. This part is my inference from the context logs, because a log can't prove why the model chose them.
3. **A refusal gives no alternatives (my code).** It only says "Choose a listed slot", without saying which slots are open. The model then invented a list, three times.
4. **The prompt encourages it (my code).** It says "list a few open slots", but nothing says to state only slots listed for that exact provider, or what to do when you push back. So when you did, it gave in and brought the made-up slots back.
5. **Nothing checks the reply.** Code checks what the model does, and checks claims that something was booked, but not what it says about availability.
6. **The model works out weekdays itself.** Slots arrive as `2026-11-10T10:00:00+05:30` with no day name. It got them right here, but that breaks our rule that the model never works out dates.

## What I ruled out
- **Memory and the assembler's trimming:** the full chat was sent, and the saved schedule was correct.
- **Tool failures:** the search returned correct data, and code refused correctly.
- **The trace panel:** the trace stores a shortened copy of each result (11 slots here), so it doesn't show what the model received. The audit used `context_log`, which does.

## Proposed fixes
1. **Send all open slots, per provider and grouped by day, with weekdays written by code.** For example: `2026-11-10 (Tue): 09:00, 10:00`. This goes in both the search result and the later-turn section. Very long date ranges would be capped by days, with a prompt to narrow the dates.
2. **Make refusals useful.** They would return that provider's real slots for that day, or the days it does have open.
3. **Tighten the prompt.**
    - State only slots listed for that exact provider.
    - If it isn't listed, it isn't open.
    - If you push back, re-read the list and don't just agree.
4. **Test it.** I'd add regression tests from this chat and replay it on live Gemini.

I wouldn't add a code check on the reply text. Matching free text against slots is fragile and would give false alarms. With the full list and useful refusals, the card stays the final check. These fixes make invented slots much less likely, but a model can still misread a list, so this won't get that risk to zero.

**You:**

cant the model query the provider tool with the exact day? instead of basically giving all of the slots to the model, can't it exactly query that particular provider by the date and the day and the time? Then there are tools are problematic, right? If we are not having that sort of functionality. And also initially, yes, initially to get available slots, it can, you know, query using the days. As well as the area, to figure out the names. It doesn't need to, you know, get all the slots in its token context.

**Claude:**

You're right, and that's a better design than my plan to send every slot. The real gap is the one you named: no tool can ask "what's open for this provider on this day?", so the model guessed.

One constraint: the brief fixes the provider's tools, and `search_providers` can't filter by provider. So I'll add our own tool, `get_open_slots(provider_id, day)`, which reads that provider's slots for that day from the stored search. The first search then returns only names, prices, ratings and which days are open. A booking still checks the slot live when it takes a hold. I'm building that now.

**Claude:**

Your design is built and running on your local stack, and in the live replay of your AC chat the agent didn't invent any slots. You were right that the tools were the problem.

## What changed
- **First search:** it returns only each provider's name, price, rating and open days, such as `2026-11-09 Mon`. No times.
- **New `get_open_slots(provider_id, day)`:** it returns one provider's times on one day.
- **Refused slots:** a refusal now lists the real times that day and the provider's open days, so the model has no reason to guess.
- **Prompt:** the model may not name a time unless the tool returned it for that exact provider in the same turn. If you dispute something, it must check again.

## Where this differs from what you described
- **It doesn't call the provider again:** the brief fixes the provider's tools, and `search_providers` can't filter by provider. So `get_open_slots` reads the stored results of the last search. A slot can go stale, but the hold still checks with the provider, and a taken slot gets refused.
- **No time filter:** you mentioned querying by time too. A day has at most about 7 slots, so the tool returns them all. `propose_booking` already checks the exact time.

## Same chat, live

| You said | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "lets go with quick" | Monday times, read from a cut-off list | Called the tool for Monday and listed the 6 real times |
| "what do you suggest" | Invented Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 | Said Quick isn't open Tuesday, listed its real days |
| "lets do tue" | Tried to book, refused | Said it isn't open Tuesday, without trying |
| "you just said they had slots on tues" | Apologised and invented six slots | Apologised and stayed correct: not open Tuesday |
| "ok wed then, lets do 11" | Not reached | Called the tool, then showed a card for Wed 11/11, 11:00, ₹1,220 |

I also asked about Trusted AC Care on Tuesday. It listed all 7 real times, and "lets do 11" gave a correct card. The ₹1,220 above is the provider's held quote against a ₹1,020 list price, and the agent pointed that out.

## What still isn't right
- **It misread your schedule:** in one reply it said you have "Wednesdays and Fridays off", when your saved schedule says office on Mon, Wed and Fri. The saved fact was correct, so this is the model's reasoning, and no tool catches it. This model is the cheap lite tier, so this may keep happening.
- **An awkward reply:** one answer corrected itself mid-sentence with "(Wait, Quick AC Care is not open...)". The content ended up right, but it reads badly.
- **The rule on naming times is prompt-only:** code checks proposals and the card shows the real slot, but nothing checks the times written in a reply. One replay proves little, though a wrong time still can't get booked.
- **Tokens didn't really drop:** the search turn used 16,389 input tokens, up from 15,232 before, because the prompt and tool list grew. Search results are smaller, but the fix mainly improves accuracy. It doesn't save tokens yet.

## Testing
I ran the affected unit test files, plus lint, types and import rules. I also changed `test_booking_saga.py`, an integration test, so CI will be its first run, along with the full suite. Nothing is committed: this is on `memory-context`, and the transcript stays uncommitted too. It's logged as bug 14 in `BUGS.md`.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:** FastAPI, PostgreSQL 17 (databases `errand`, `adk_sessions`, `mock_provider`, plus `*_test`), Redis 8, Google ADK 2.13.0 (thin), Gemini `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (free tier 15 requests/min), React + Vite + TS served by nginx, Docker Compose (`make up`), Alembic, taskiq + `RedisStreamBroker`.
   - **Layout (user decided):** domain-led with standard FastAPI files (`router.py`, `schemas.py`, `models.py`, `repository.py`, `service.py`), shared code in `app/core/`. Routers have no DB access, services own transactions, repositories only flush, no transaction across network calls, fakes only at infra boundaries. `.importlinter` now has 7 contracts.
   - **Core rule:** model can only read and propose. Only deterministic code changes a booking, after an approval the model cannot produce.
   - **Approval flow:** `propose_booking` (model tool, local) → checks shortlist → `hold_slot` (Caller.PROPOSAL) → approval row with SHA-256 hash over action, user, provider_id, provider_name, slot, price, list_price, currency, hold_id, expires_at → card from row only. Yes/no read from raw whole message (`read_decision`) or click, before the model runs. Confirm is one transaction: conditional consume, workflow → EXECUTING, attempt row with key `book:<approval_id>`, outbox job `bookings.run_attempt`. Publish last, after `finish_run`.
   - **Saga (`BookingSaga`, worker):** claim attempt with lease and `claims` fence; read `get_provider` price; `token_for(approval, current_price)` = `"<approval_id>:<hash of facts with current list price>"`; commit `book_calls` before call; `book`; always VERIFYING + `get_booking_status`; only that reports success. Results: booked → DONE + template notification; slot_taken → COMPARING with other slots; timeout+not booked → retry same key, MAX_BOOK_CALLS=3; hold_expired/price change → new hold + fresh approval (`_ask_again`); status unavailable or job limit/fault → stays open, "not confirmed yet" once; sweep `recover()` requeues open attempts with no live lease when `queued_at` is older than the lease.
   - **Verifier:** `BookingApprovalVerifier.is_valid` checks consumed, user, action, hold, key, row hash, current hash; attempt must be open. `DenyAllApprovals` kept for tests.
   - **PostgreSQL is truth, Redis only carries work.** Only `api` writes ADK sessions; workers write `errand`; model reads booking news through `prompt_note`. Saga events continue the run that took the yes (`resume_run`, `settle_run`, seq clash retry).
   - **Polling before SSE:** UI polls `/notifications` every 2 s while a booking runs; TracePanel refreshes while outcome is `verifying`.
   - **Date rules:** "Saturday" counts today; "next Saturday" never today; **"next weekend" = coming Sat/Sun, never today (user decided)**; later weekends need exact dates; "next week" = next calendar week. A yes that adds a detail is clear even after two questions; plain yes after two questions gets direct question; "yes, Sunday" → OTHER.
   - **Testing practice:** unit (real mock via ASGI, real ADK loop with `ScriptedLlm`, SQLite, fakeredis), integration in Compose (`make test-integration`), `make smoke`, live Gemini scripts, headless Chromium, deliberate-break audits.

**Claude:**

Both problems are fixed. **Reload your tab once before retesting**, because it's still running old code. Then click **New chat**: the card in your old chat ran out at 07:16, so it won't come back, and the agent should treat that 11:00 slot as free again.

## Where the card went
The server did create it, and your approval row is there. Your tab never showed it because it was still running the build from before the card existed. The web logs show no asset requests from your browser until after that turn, and I never saw the old code run, so this is inferred from the logs. The old code dropped the card from the reply, so even a reload couldn't bring it back.

Reloading only fixes your tab, so I also made the card harder to lose:
- **Recovery on load:** the page now asks the server what's open, so it can recover a missed card or a running booking. A card the server has closed also closes on the page.
- **Fresh builds:** a reload now always picks up the latest build.
- **Failed turns:** a turn that fails now still returns any open card.

## What happened with "yes, and im in indiranagar"
Three things went wrong in a row:
1. **Two questions at once:** Gemini asked about the dates and your area together, even though the prompt says not to. It still does this sometimes, as the replay below showed.
2. **My date rule was too strict:** it treated any yes after two questions as unclear, even yours, which clearly answered both.
3. **A false failure message:** Gemini saved your area but wrote no text, so you got "Nothing was changed", which was untrue.

The fixes:
- **Date answers:**

| You say, after two questions | Result |
|---|---|
| `yes, and im in indiranagar` | Dates confirmed |
| `yes` | Asks directly about the dates |
| `yes, what's the price?` | Asks directly about the dates |
| `yes, Sunday` | Not a yes to Saturday. This was also wrong before, even when the dates were the only question |

- **Empty replies:** if Gemini writes nothing, code now asks the next question from what's saved. It only counts as a failure when there's nothing to ask.
- **Failure messages:** they now say "This message did not make or change any booking". If a booking is running, they say that instead of denying it.

## One more thing from your screenshot
When you said "uh no sharma", Gemini picked 11:00 for you, though you never chose a slot. The prompt now tells it to list slots and ask, unless you say something like "the earliest". That's only guidance, so it may still happen. The card is still what protects you, since nothing books until you confirm those exact details.

## Proof
- **Your conversation replayed:** headless Chromium on live Gemini went from your first message to a verified booking. Gemini asked its two questions again, and your yes went straight through to the search.
- **Lost card:** in that same run I removed the card from the page's saved chat and reloaded. The card came back, and clicking **Confirm** booked it.
- **Tests:** 829 server, 38 UI and 26 integration tests pass, and all 12 deliberate breaks of the new rules were caught.

These are numbers 9 and 10 in `BUGS.md`. Both came from your testing, so they'd make good entries for the "three real bugs" deliverable. The stack is still in eval mode, so the test commands from my last message still work.

**Claude:**

The "Are these dates okay?" question is gone. If your date words are clear, the agent saves them and searches straight away. I went a step further than changing the wording, since you said to trust the user and the card already checks before booking. **Reload your tab and start a new chat to try it.**

## How your chat runs now (live Gemini)
| You say | Agent replies |
|---|---|
| Find a plumber for my kitchen tap this week, mornings only, under ₹1,500. | `Dates: This week (03/11/2026 to 08/11/2026).` Which area are you in? |
| indiranagar and yes dates look fine, make it on friday | For this Friday (06/11/2026) morning, I found 7 plumbers in Indiranagar… |

## The new rules
- **Clear date:** saved with no question, and the search runs in the same turn.
- **No date or vague date:** it still asks, now in its own words. For example: "When would you like the electrician to come?"
- **Pressure to skip:** "Just search, do not ask me anything" still gets the question if there is no date.
- **Change of date:** "No, Sunday instead" saves Sunday and searches again. If a card is open, it closes.
- **Exact dates are always shown:** if Gemini leaves them out, code adds a `Dates:` line, as in the first reply above. This is how you spot a wrong reading before the card.
- **Dates still come from code:** Gemini can't work out a date, and words you never said are refused.

## Known limits
- **Unsure dates:** "maybe Saturday?" searched Saturday without asking, even though the prompt says to ask. It books nothing and shows the date, so I left it. Code could catch these words and force a question if you want.
- **Dates said in passing:** "I was away last Saturday" could be read as the request date, because only the prompt guards this now. Gemini handled it correctly in the one run I tried, and it asked when.

## Proof
- **Live chats:** seven chats on live Gemini behaved as above, apart from the "maybe Saturday" case.
- **Real UI:** your chat in headless Chromium went through the card to a verified booking for Fri 06/11/2026, 10:00, ₹600, with no browser errors.
- **Tests:** 749 server, 38 UI and 26 integration tests pass. The server count fell from 829 because most of the removed tests covered the old yes/no date reading.
- **Deliberate breaks:** all 12 are now caught. One got through at first, a date range shown with only one end, so I added a test for it.

`BUILD_LOG.md`, `BUGS.md` and the server notes are updated. Bug 9 in `BUGS.md` now says the date question is gone; its empty-reply and failure-reply fixes stay.

Add approvals and the booking saga

The model can only propose a booking. A card built from the approval row
shows the exact provider, slot and price, and only a click or a whole-message
yes approves it, read before the model runs. The saga books with a token
bound to the approved facts, and only get_booking_status can report success.

- Approvals: hold, hash, one conditional consume, void on any change.
- Saga: claim with a lease, retry with the same key, recover through the sweep.
- Notifications: template text written when an attempt closes, polled by the UI.
- UI: approval card, booking progress, and recovery of an open card on load.
- Dates: clear words are saved with no question. The reply must show the exact
  dates, and code adds them if the model leaves them out.
EOF

**In short:** the agent can now really book. It collects details, compares providers within the user's limits, holds a slot and shows a card with the exact details. Only the user's click or whole-message yes approves it. A worker then books, always checks the provider's status, and only then reports success. It cannot cancel, reschedule or remember anything across sessions yet.

**Claude:**

It's slow because of the deliberate-break audit, not the normal tests. The normal tests are quick.

| Step | Tests | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Deliberate breaks** | 30 breaks, each followed by a rerun of the booking, workflow and agent unit tests | Up to about 15 minutes (my estimate) |
| **`make check`** | 819 server unit tests and 40 UI tests, plus lint, types and import rules | About 1 minute |
| **`make test-integration`** | 30 tests with real PostgreSQL, Redis and worker processes | About 2 minutes |

- **Why the audit takes so long:** the full unit suite takes about 36 seconds, and each break reruns part of it. A rerun stops at the first failure, so a caught break finishes early. A break the tests miss takes the longest, because every selected test has to run.
- **What it's for:** it checks that the tests really catch the rule being broken. Each break changes one rule, such as reporting success without checking the provider, and at least one test must fail.
- **Other slow runs:** the live Gemini run also took several minutes, because I wait 13 seconds between messages to stay inside the free-tier rate limit. That one is already finished.

A count I just started is also still running, and it's competing with the audit for the machine. The server count above comes from the last full run, and the UI count adds the two tests I wrote after it. I'll report the audit and test results when they finish.

**Claude:**

Yes, your local Docker is up to date. I checked that `api` and `worker` are running the new saga code and that the web bundle has the new cards. **Reload your tab and click New chat before testing.**

The integration tests are still finishing, and a `make up` runs right after them. No app code has changed since the last build, so it shouldn't change anything, but the app could blip for a moment.

The UI runs as `demo-user`, who has an upcoming AC servicing booking, so you can start straight away. Try these in order, because the last one cancels that booking:

| Say | What should happen |
|---|---|
| `Move my AC servicing to next week` | It asks which day and time, and shows no card |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 10am` | A "Move this booking?" card shows the current and new times |
| `keep it` | The booking stays as it is |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 12 noon`, then `yes` | Conflict: "your booking did not move", and it stays where it was |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 10am`, then Confirm | "Moved and verified", with both times |
| `Cancel my AC servicing` | A "Cancel this booking?" card appears |
| `book it` | Ignored as an answer, and the card stays open |
| `cancel it` | "Cancelled and verified" |

**What you may run into:**
- **Provider not working that hour:** the provider doesn't work about a quarter of its hours, and I can't check this before the card. Only after you confirm will you see "does not work at…", and your booking stays put. This can hit either the 10am or the noon move, so just try another hour. If noon gets this message, you've seen the failure path but not the conflict.
- **Other slots:** after a conflict, it only suggests other slots if a search in that chat listed them. Otherwise it asks you for another time.

To test on a booking you just made, use the normal flow: search, book, then say `Cancel my plumber booking`.

.PHONY: up down logs reset ps test test-web test-integration check smoke web-dev transcript

up:

down:

logs:

**Claude:**

The full check is now in GitHub CI, but it won't run until this branch is pushed, so it's untested on GitHub. It's in [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) and runs on every pull request and every push to `main`, with no secrets needed.

| Job | What it runs |
|---|---|
| **Server** | Lint, format, types, import rules and all unit tests |
| **Web** | Types, tests and build |
| **Integration** | `make test-integration`, with real PostgreSQL, Redis and workers in Compose |

- **Workflow file:** it passes `actionlint`.
- **Clean-copy run:** I ran the server and web steps on a copy of the repo with no keys or local settings. That caught a real problem: 6 tests in `test_model_retry.py` only passed here because your machine has a real `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. That key was also being sent to the local fake model server in those tests, though it never left your machine.
- **The fix:** those tests now use a fake key. I reran those 6 in the clean environment and they pass, but I didn't repeat the whole server step.
- **Integration job:** it has only run here through `make test-integration`, not on a clean copy.
- **Minutes:** the repo is private, so each run uses your GitHub Actions minutes.

Your day and time fixes are live on the rebuilt stack, so you can retest whenever you like. Reload your tab and start a new chat.

**Claude:**

No, this doesn't look like rate limiting. A rate limit would show up as a `429` error, and we aren't getting any. What we're seeing is slow replies and `504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` timeouts, which means Gemini accepted the request but didn't finish in time.

- **No 429s in the logs:** a search of the last 15–20 minutes of API logs found no `429` or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors. The lines that matched were just timestamps and code line numbers containing "429".
- **No rate-limit events in the traces:** the app records `model_rate_limited` when Gemini refuses a call for this reason, and there are none in the last 3 hours.
- **Well under the limit:** our busiest recent minute was 7 model calls, against the free tier's 15 requests a minute.
- **Still slow:** a tiny "Say ok." call just now succeeded but took 29.7 seconds, compared with the usual 1–2 seconds for our full calls. A refused call fails right away, so this doesn't look like a refusal.

**What I can't rule out:** Google could be slowing free-tier traffic without sending an error, and that would look the same from here. Either way, it's on Gemini's side and our call volume doesn't seem to be the cause. Waiting is the simplest fix.

"""Per-session turn lock on Redis.

ADK rejects a write from anyone holding an older copy of a session, so two turns on one session
must not overlap. The lock has an owner token and an expiry longer than the run deadline. If it
ever expires early, ADK's StaleSessionError is the backstop.
"""

import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

from redis.asyncio import Redis
from redis.exceptions import LockError, LockNotOwnedError, RedisError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TurnLockTimeout(Exception):
    """Another turn held the session for the whole wait."""


class TurnLockUnavailable(Exception):
    """Redis could not be reached, so the turn fails closed."""


class RedisTurnLock:
    def __init__(self, redis: Redis, ttl_s: float, wait_s: float) -> None:
        self._redis = redis
        self._ttl_s = ttl_s
        self._wait_s = wait_s

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def hold(self, key: str) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        lock = self._redis.lock(f"turn-lock:{key}", timeout=self._ttl_s, sleep=0.05)
        try:
            acquired = await lock.acquire(blocking_timeout=self._wait_s)
        except (RedisError, OSError) as error:
            raise TurnLockUnavailable(str(error)) from error
        if not acquired:
            raise TurnLockTimeout(key)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await self._release(lock, key)

    async def _release(self, lock: Any

"""Tells the api that a user has news. Only a wake-up: the news itself is in PostgreSQL.

A lost wake-up costs a short delay, because every reader also looks again on a timer. So Redis being
down slows delivery and loses nothing.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any

from redis.asyncio import Redis
from redis.exceptions import RedisError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _channel(user_id: str) -> str:
    return f"news:{user_id}"


class WakeupListener:
    def __init__(self, redis: Redis, channel: str) -> None:
        self._redis = redis
        self._channel = channel
        self._pubsub: Any | None = None

    async def _subscribe(self) -> None:
        try:
            pubsub = self._redis.pubsub()
            await pubsub.subscribe(self._channel)
            self._pubsub = pubsub
        except (RedisError, OSError):
            logger.warning("could not subscribe to %s", self._channel)
            self._pubsub = None

    async def wait(self, timeout_s: float) -> bool:
        """True if a wake-up came. False can also mean Redis is down, which the timer covers."""
        if self._pubsub is None:
            await self._subscribe()
        if self._pubsub is None:
            await asyncio.sleep(timeout_s)

"""One JSONL file per run. api and worker append to the same file, so one booking is one trace.

A file write failure must never change a user's outcome. PostgreSQL still has the trace.
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import re
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from app.core.redaction import scrub_value

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class JsonlTraceFiles:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | Path, process: str) -> None:
        self._directory = Path(directory)
        self._process = process

    def path_for(self, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> Path:
        return self._directory / f"{run_id}.jsonl"

    def append(self, run_id: uuid.UUID, line: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        record = {"run_id": str(run_id), "process": self._process, **line}
        data = (json.dumps(record, default=str, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode()
        try:
            self._directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # One write on an append-only descriptor, so two processes cannot mix their lines.
            descriptor = os.open(self.path_for(run_id), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT)
            try:
                os.write(descriptor, data)
            finally:
                os.close(descriptor)
        except OSError:
            logger.warning("could not write the trace file for run %s", run_id, exc_info=True)

Your usage limit was reached, so I stopped with step 7 only partly done. The server side is written, but the UI work and live testing are still left. Everything is uncommitted on the branch `proactive-sse-jsonl`, and [PR 8](https://github.com/AviroopPaul/orange-assignment/pull/8) was already merged.

**Done (server only):**
- **Detection:** a poll every 20 s compares `list_bookings` with our records, and code decides whether to notify and records why. A repeat or a past booking gets no notice. The code is in [policy.py](server/app/domains/proactive/policy.py) and [service.py](server/app/domains/proactive/service.py).
- **Replacements:**
  - **Search:** it stays within the saved request and leaves out the provider that cancelled.
  - **Rebooking:** it holds no slot, so rebooking still goes through a fresh approval card.
  - **Running turns:** a turn in progress delays reopening the errand, but not the cancel notice.
  - **Other errands:** another errand already open in that chat is left alone.
- **SSE:** `GET /events` replays stored notifications after the cursor, then pushes new ones on a Redis wake-up.
- **JSONL:** api and worker write to one file per run under `./artifacts/traces`, and forgetting a fact scrubs those files too.

**Checked:**
- **Tests:** 127 unit tests pass across [test_proactive.py](server/tests/unit/test_proactive.py), the broker, tracing and architecture files. Only the new file covers this build, and I didn't run the full suite.
- **Static checks:** ruff, mypy and the import rules all pass.

**Left to do:**
1. **Web UI:** replace the `/notifications` polling in [useChat.ts](web/src/domains/chat/useChat.ts) with `EventSource`, and update the three App tests that fake the polling. Until then, users won't see a provider cancel in the chat. The UI also needs to:
   - close any card listed in `closed_cards`
   - hold notices back while a turn is running
   - keep the cursor when you start a new chat
   - show notices from another session, with a way to open that chat
2. **Live run:** rebuild with `make up`, which applies the new migration, then run `alembic check`. After that, do a real booking, trigger a provider cancel and rebook through the card.
3. **Other tests:** add an integration test for E24 and E25, and confirm the JSONL file holds both api and worker lines from a real run. No test covers the live `/events` route or the Redis push yet; the unit test only checks replay after the cursor.
4. **Docs:**
   - Move the F12, E24, E25 and N13 statuses once there is live proof. I added a log entry to `BUILD_LOG.md` but left those statuses unchanged.
   - Add this section to "Changes from the blueprint", which I haven't done yet: each reader also rechecks every 10 s, so Redis being down only slows delivery.
   - Add `proactive` and the new rules to `server/app/CLAUDE.md`.

**Known limits to log:** only bookings made or changed through this system are watched, so a cancel on a seeded demo booking stays silent. If another errand is open, the user is told about the cancel but gets no replacement list until they ask.

# Real bugs hit while building

Candidates for the "three real bugs" deliverable. Each one really happened, and each has a test that guards it.

## 1. A killed worker's job never came back on a quiet queue

- **What broke:** After `kill -9` on a worker mid-job, the job stayed undelivered. With a 5 s idle timeout it had still not returned after 40 s.
- **Why:** In `taskiq-redis`, the reclaim step comes after `if not fetched: continue`. So it only runs when a new job arrives. On a quiet queue, it never runs.
- **Fix:** Recovery no longer depends on the broker. Jobs have leases in PostgreSQL, and a sweep every 15 s requeues expired ones.
- **Regression test:** `test_killed_worker_on_a_quiet_queue_recovers_through_the_sweep` in `server/tests/integration/test_worker_recovery.py`.

**Claude:**

Step 7 is finished: provider-cancel detection, SSE in the chat and JSONL traces all work on the running stack. Nothing is committed yet. It's all on `proactive-sse-jsonl`, and the transcript files are still left out of any commit.

**What now happens**
- **Provider cancels:** within about 20 s the user gets a notice in the chat with no prompt. A second notice then lists up to 3 replacements that fit their saved request.
- **Rebooking:** no slot is held, and picking a replacement shows a new approval card.
- **Chat news:** the chat now gets news through `/events` instead of polling, and a reconnect replays anything it missed. The trace panel still polls while a run is open, because most trace events create no notification.
- **Trace files:** each run gets one file in `artifacts/traces/`, written by both api and worker. Forgetting a fact scrubs these files too.

**Checked live**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Book with real Gemini, then provider cancels | 1 cancel notice and 1 replacement notice over SSE |
| Two more polls | No new notice; 2 repeats recorded |
| Reconnect with a cursor | Replayed exactly the 2 missed notices |
| Pick a replacement | New card and no new booking attempt; the cancelling provider was not offered |
| Trace files against the database | One line per event plus a first `run_started` line; the booking run has both api and worker lines |
| Real UI through nginx, headless | News appeared with no reload, and still only once after a reload |
| Redis stopped with a stream open | A notice added by hand arrived in 10 s; the stack recovered after restart |

**Bugs found**
- **Wrong reply after booking:** "thanks" after a verified booking got "please confirm the card", because the model's chat history never showed the system's news. That news is now in its history, and the reply was correct in the one live rerun. It's bug 15 in `BUGS.md`.
- **Stream opening:** the stream reported "no news" as soon as it opened. Users wouldn't have noticed, and it's fixed.
- **My own slip:** I ran Prettier at the wrong line width, which reflowed files I hadn't meant to change. I re-ran it at width 100, which removed that churn.

**Tests run**
- **Passing:** the new unit and integration tests for this step, the memory, runtime, broker, tracing and architecture unit tests, and all 48 web tests. `alembic check` is clean.
- **Full server suite:** not run; GitHub CI will run it on the PR.

**Not tested**
- A worker killed on real processes between the cancel notice and the replacements. A unit test holding the turn lock shows a later poll finishes the job.
- A real chat turn running during a cancel; that test only holds the lock.
- Clicking "Open that chat" in the real UI; only a UI test covers it.

To try it yourself, book something in the chat at `localhost:3000`, then run this with your booking ID:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8100/admin/provider-cancel -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"booking_id":"bkg-..."}'
```

The new design choices are in `BUILD_LOG.md`, under "Changes from the blueprint" and "Known limits of proactive detection". The main limits are that only bookings made or changed through this system are watched, and that the replacement list waits if another errand is open in that chat. E24 and E25 stay Partial until the eval harness in step 8.

**Claude:**

The stack is now running `gemini-3.6-flash` at `localhost:3000`, ready for you to test. I stopped the background check, so there's no more `gemini-3.8-flash` data beyond its three 503 errors.

**What changed**
- **Model:** it's now the default in `config.py`, `compose.yaml` and `.env.example`. The api and worker containers both report the new model.
- **Images:** I rebuilt the server and test images. The web image is 58 minutes old because Docker reused its cached build, as nothing in `web/` has changed since then.
- **Eval mode:** I kept it on, so the provider-cancel `curl` still works.

**What to expect**
- **It may not feel faster:** my one real chat turn took 22.9 s for a single model call with 3,793 input tokens. The last `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` call in the traces took 21.6 s with 5,344 input tokens. That's one call each, so it doesn't settle anything, but a turn with several model calls could still be slow.
- **Not tested:** the booking flow hasn't run on this model yet. Your test will be the first time, including how well it follows the rules on dates and times.
- **Cost shows as unknown:** `pricing.py` has no price for this model, and I didn't want to guess one. The cost field stays blank until a real price is added.

To go back, run this:

```bash
MODEL_NAME=gemini-3.5-flash-lite MOCK_EVAL_MODE=true make up
```

If it's still slow, try lowering its thinking level next, since it was using 79 to 173 thinking tokens even on a tiny prompt. I haven't tested whether that helps. Nothing is committed, and the model switch is noted in `BUILD_LOG.md`.

**openai/gpt-oss-120b on Groq**

- **Context window:** 131,072 tokens

Result:

```
**Rate limits for openai/gpt-oss-120b** (base Developer plan figures; the page doesn't list separate free-tier numbers for this model):

- **RPM:** 30
- **RPD:** 1K
- **TPM:** 8K
- **TPD:** 200K
- **ASH:** not applicable
- **ASD:** not applicable

**How the limits work:**

- Limits apply to your organization, not to individual users.
- Any limit can be hit first. The docs give an example: with an RPM of 50 and a TPM of 200K, sending 50 tiny requests in one minute hits the limit even though far fewer than 200K tokens were used.
- When you exceed a limit, the API returns HTTP 429 with the status text "Too Many Requests."
- The `retry-after` header gives the wait time in seconds. It is set only when a 429 is returned.
- Cached tokens do not count toward your rate limits.
```

**Claude:**

**We can use Groq's `gpt-oss-120b`, but not reliably on the free tier.** The model is very fast, about 1 s per call, but our token use is far above the free limits. Light manual testing would work, with long pauses. The eval runs would not.

**Free tier limits against our real use**

The limits come from Groq's docs, and your key's response headers confirm the 8,000 and 1,000 figures. Our use comes from 524 logged model calls and 253 turns, converted to Groq's count (see the next section).

| Limit | Free tier | Our use, in Groq tokens | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokens per minute | 8,000 | About 2,900 per average call, 4,900 at p95; a turn averages about 6,000, and 13,300 at p95 | **Fails** |
| Tokens per day | 200,000 | About 1.43M today | **Fails: about 7 times over** |
| Requests per day | 1,000 | 508 today | Fits |
| Requests per minute | 30 | 11 at our busiest | Fits |

- **Daily room:** 200,000 tokens is only about 33 average turns a day.
- **Busy minutes:** 83 of the 107 minutes with model calls used more than 8,000 tokens, counted in Gemini tokens. Our busiest minute used about 51,000.

**What the replay showed**

I replayed 2 real logged test turns (6 model calls) using our real prompts and tools.

- **Token size:** Groq counts about 18% fewer input tokens than Gemini for the same request, for example 4,068 against 5,018.
- **Speed:** each call took 0.6 to 1.5 s. Gemini took 7 to 20 s on a much smaller prompt, so that comparison is only rough.
- **Waiting:** the whole replay took 125 s, and 119 s of that was waiting after 8 rate-limit errors. One 4,000-token call uses about 30 s of the allowance.
- **Our code would break:** two waits were 31 s and 34 s, over our 30 s limit (`model_rate_limit_max_wait_s`), so the user would get a "busy" reply. Our largest logged turn would need about 100 s of waiting, close to the 120 s run deadline.
- **Caching doesn't help:** cached tokens don't count against the limit, but Groq reported 0 cached tokens on all 9 calls, including the same prompt sent 3 times.
- **Tool choice:** it picked sensible tools in the replay, such as `get_open_slots` and `propose_booking`. That's only 6 calls on logged history, not a full booking on Groq.

**Why trimming won't fix it**

Tools and the system prompt alone are about 4,800 of our estimated tokens on every call. Even a much smaller prompt would still limit us to about 3 calls a minute, and an average turn already makes 2.1 calls.

**Options**
- **Groq on a paid tier (my pick if speed matters most):**
  - The price is $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output, so an average turn costs about $0.001.
  - I couldn't confirm the paid limits, so check them before you pay.
  - It also needs a new model adapter for ADK (the agent framework) and new rate-limit handling, plus a price entry and a rerun of the live flows.
- **Stay on Gemini:** no new code is needed, but it stays slow and uneven, and `gemini-3.6-flash` is still only lightly tested.
- **Groq free tier, for a short demo only:** a demo fits the daily limit, but 30 s pauses would show on screen. It also still needs the adapter.

The eval runs could also be a problem on the free tier. If each of the 36 scenarios took about 3 live turns, that's roughly 650,000 tokens, or more than 3 days of the daily limit. This is my estimate, since the harness isn't built yet. You could avoid that by running most evals with the scripted model.

**Claude:**

Yes, an older model looks workable. **`gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-3-flash-preview` were both fast and got the tool call right every time.** Both took about 1.5 s per call, while most of the other models failed with errors.

I sent each model the same short prompt with one small tool, 4 times, about 70 input tokens per call. A call counted as correct only if it used the tool with both the right service and the right area.

| Model | Correct calls | Median time | Range | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemini-3-flash-preview` | 4 of 4 | 1.3 s | 1.2 to 1.7 s | Fast and reliable |
| `gemini-2.5-flash` | 4 of 4 | 1.5 s | 1.2 to 1.8 s | Fast and reliable |
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | 3 of 4 | 34.2 s | 3.5 to 39.1 s | Very slow, plus one 503 |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | All 503 (high demand) |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | Three 503s and one timeout |
| `gemini-3.7-flash` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | All 503 |
| `gemini-omni-1.1-flash` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | All 429 (quota) |
| `gemini-omni-flash-preview` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | All 429 (quota) |
| `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | 0 of 4 | n/a | n/a | 404, Google no longer offers it to this key |

For comparison, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` took 1.2 to 20.1 s and `gemini-3.6-flash` took 7 to 13 s in the earlier small check, though that used a slightly different prompt and tool.

**I'd pick `gemini-2.5-flash`:**
- **Not a preview:** `gemini-3-flash-preview` is a preview model, which is riskier to depend on for a demo.
- **Cost tracking works:** `pricing.py` already has its price, so cost shows up in the traces with no extra work.
- **Speed is about the same:** the 0.2 s gap between the two is too small to matter in a test this size.

**What this doesn't prove:**
- **Busy periods:** all of this ran over a few minutes, and the 503s suggest demand changes. A model that's fast now may not stay that way.
- **Real turns:** our real calls are about 3,500 input tokens with 13 tools, roughly 50 times this size. So 1.5 s is a best case.
- **Rule following:** one simple tool call doesn't show whether it follows our rules on dates, times and approval cards. Those rules are where weaker models could slip, so that's the main thing to check next.
- **Free tier limits:** I didn't check the limits for these two models. They could matter as much as speed, as they did with Groq.

If you switch, I'd change the default, rebuild and run the live booking script once. That would measure real turn speed and check the rules on a full booking, provider cancel and rebook.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:** FastAPI, PostgreSQL 17 (databases `errand`, `adk_sessions`, `mock_provider`, plus `*_test`), Redis 8, Google ADK 2.13.0 (thin), Gemini `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (free tier 15 requests/min), React + Vite + TS served by nginx, Docker Compose (`make up`), Alembic, taskiq + `RedisStreamBroker`.
   - **Layout (user decided):** domain-led with standard FastAPI files (`router.py`, `schemas.py`, `models.py`, `repository.py`, `service.py`), shared code in `app/core/`. Routers have no DB access, services own transactions, repositories only flush, no transaction across network calls, fakes only at infra boundaries. `.importlinter` now has 7 contracts.
   - **Core rule:** model can only read and propose. Only deterministic code changes a booking, after an approval the model cannot produce.
   - **Approval flow:** `propose_booking` (model tool, local) → checks shortlist → `hold_slot` (Caller.PROPOSAL) → approval row with SHA-256 hash over action, user, provider_id, provider_name, slot, price, list_price, currency, hold_id, expires_at → card from row only. Yes/no read from raw whole message (`read_decision`) or click, before the model runs. Confirm is one transaction: conditional consume, workflow → EXECUTING, attempt row with key `book:<approval_id>`, outbox job `bookings.run_attempt`. Publish last, after `finish_run`.
   - **Saga (`BookingSaga`, worker):** claim attempt with lease and `claims` fence; read `get_provider` price; `token_for(approval, current_price)` = `"<approval_id>:<hash of facts with current list price>"`; commit `book_calls` before call; `book`; always VERIFYING + `get_booking_status`; only that reports success. Results: booked → DONE + template notification; slot_taken → COMPARING with other slots; timeout+not booked → retry same key, MAX_BOOK_CALLS=3; hold_expired/price change → new hold + fresh approval (`_ask_again`); status unavailable or job limit/fault → stays open, "not confirmed yet" once; sweep `recover()` requeues open attempts with no live lease when `queued_at` is older than the lease.
   - **Verifier:** `BookingApprovalVerifier.is_valid` checks consumed, user, action, hold, key, row hash, current hash; attempt must be open. `DenyAllApprovals` kept for tests.
   - **PostgreSQL is truth, Redis only carries work.** Only `api` writes ADK sessions; workers write `errand`; model reads booking news through `prompt_note`. Saga events continue the run that took the yes (`resume_run`, `settle_run`, seq clash retry).
   - **Polling before SSE:** UI polls `/notifications` every 2 s while a booking runs; TracePanel refreshes while outcome is `verifying`.
   - **Date rules:** "Saturday" counts today; "next Saturday" never today; **"next weekend" = coming Sat/Sun, never today (user decided)**; later weekends need exact dates; "next week" = next calendar week. A yes that adds a detail is clear even after two questions; plain yes after two questions gets direct question; "yes, Sunday" → OTHER.
   - **Testing practice:** unit (real mock via ASGI, real ADK loop with `ScriptedLlm`, SQLite, fakeredis), integration in Compose (`make test-integration`), `make smoke`, live Gemini scripts, headless Chromium, deliberate-break audits.

**Claude:**

Both problems are fixed. **Reload your tab once before retesting**, because it's still running old code. Then click **New chat**: the card in your old chat ran out at 07:16, so it won't come back, and the agent should treat that 11:00 slot as free again.

## Where the card went
The server did create it, and your approval row is there. Your tab never showed it because it was still running the build from before the card existed. The web logs show no asset requests from your browser until after that turn, and I never saw the old code run, so this is inferred from the logs. The old code dropped the card from the reply, so even a reload couldn't bring it back.

Reloading only fixes your tab, so I also made the card harder to lose:
- **Recovery on load:** the page now asks the server what's open, so it can recover a missed card or a running booking. A card the server has closed also closes on the page.
- **Fresh builds:** a reload now always picks up the latest build.
- **Failed turns:** a turn that fails now still returns any open card.

## What happened with "yes, and im in indiranagar"
Three things went wrong in a row:
1. **Two questions at once:** Gemini asked about the dates and your area together, even though the prompt says not to. It still does this sometimes, as the replay below showed.
2. **My date rule was too strict:** it treated any yes after two questions as unclear, even yours, which clearly answered both.
3. **A false failure message:** Gemini saved your area but wrote no text, so you got "Nothing was changed", which was untrue.

The fixes:
- **Date answers:**

| You say, after two questions | Result |
|---|---|
| `yes, and im in indiranagar` | Dates confirmed |
| `yes` | Asks directly about the dates |
| `yes, what's the price?` | Asks directly about the dates |
| `yes, Sunday` | Not a yes to Saturday. This was also wrong before, even when the dates were the only question |

- **Empty replies:** if Gemini writes nothing, code now asks the next question from what's saved. It only counts as a failure when there's nothing to ask.
- **Failure messages:** they now say "This message did not make or change any booking". If a booking is running, they say that instead of denying it.

## One more thing from your screenshot
When you said "uh no sharma", Gemini picked 11:00 for you, though you never chose a slot. The prompt now tells it to list slots and ask, unless you say something like "the earliest". That's only guidance, so it may still happen. The card is still what protects you, since nothing books until you confirm those exact details.

- **Tests:** 829 server, 38 UI and 26 integration tests pass, and all 12 deliberate breaks of the new rules were caught.

**Claude:**

The "Are these dates okay?" question is gone. If your date words are clear, the agent saves them and searches straight away. I went a step further than changing the wording, since you said to trust the user and the card already checks before booking. **Reload your tab and start a new chat to try it.**

## How your chat runs now (live Gemini)
| You say | Agent replies |
|---|---|
| Find a plumber for my kitchen tap this week, mornings only, under ₹1,500. | `Dates: This week (03/11/2026 to 08/11/2026).` Which area are you in? |
| indiranagar and yes dates look fine, make it on friday | For this Friday (06/11/2026) morning, I found 7 plumbers in Indiranagar… |

## The new rules
- **Clear date:** saved with no question, and the search runs in the same turn.
- **No date or vague date:** it still asks, now in its own words. For example: "When would you like the electrician to come?"
- **Pressure to skip:** "Just search, do not ask me anything" still gets the question if there is no date.
- **Change of date:** "No, Sunday instead" saves Sunday and searches again. If a card is open, it closes.
- **Exact dates are always shown:** if Gemini leaves them out, code adds a `Dates:` line, as in the first reply above. This is how you spot a wrong reading before the card.
- **Dates still come from code:** Gemini can't work out a date, and words you never said are refused.

## Known limits
- **Unsure dates:** "maybe Saturday?" searched Saturday without asking, even though the prompt says to ask. It books nothing and shows the date, so I left it. Code could catch these words and force a question if you want.
- **Dates said in passing:** "I was away last Saturday" could be read as the request date, because only the prompt guards this now. Gemini handled it correctly in the one run I tried, and it asked when.

## Proof
- **Live chats:** seven chats on live Gemini behaved as above, apart from the "maybe Saturday" case.
- **Real UI:** your chat in headless Chromium went through the card to a verified booking for Fri 06/11/2026, 10:00, ₹600, with no browser errors.
- **Tests:** 749 server, 38 UI and 26 integration tests pass. The server count fell from 829 because most of the removed tests covered the old yes/no date reading.
- **Deliberate breaks:** all 12 are now caught. One got through at first, a date range shown with only one end, so I added a test for it.

`BUILD_LOG.md`, `BUGS.md` and the server notes are updated. Bug 9 in `BUGS.md` now says the date question is gone; its empty-reply and failure-reply fixes stay.

Add approvals and the booking saga

The model can only propose a booking. A card built from the approval row
shows the exact provider, slot and price, and only a click or a whole-message
yes approves it, read before the model runs. The saga books with a token

  dates, and code adds them if the model leaves them out.
EOF

@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool", ["book", "cancel", "reschedule"])
def test_consequential_tools_need_approval_and_only_the_saga_can_call_them(tool: str) -> None:

def test_model_can_only_reach_read_tools() -> None:

**Claude:**

It's slow because of the deliberate-break audit, not the normal tests. The normal tests are quick.

| Step | Tests | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Deliberate breaks** | 30 breaks, each followed by a rerun of the booking, workflow and agent unit tests | Up to about 15 minutes (my estimate) |
| **`make check`** | 819 server unit tests and 40 UI tests, plus lint, types and import rules | About 1 minute |
| **`make test-integration`** | 30 tests with real PostgreSQL, Redis and worker processes | About 2 minutes |

- **Why the audit takes so long:** the full unit suite takes about 36 seconds, and each break reruns part of it. A rerun stops at the first failure, so a caught break finishes early. A break the tests miss takes the longest, because every selected test has to run.
- **What it's for:** it checks that the tests really catch the rule being broken. Each break changes one rule, such as reporting success without checking the provider, and at least one test must fail.
- **Other slow runs:** the live Gemini run also took several minutes, because I wait 13 seconds between messages to stay inside the free-tier rate limit. That one is already finished.

A count I just started is also still running, and it's competing with the audit for the machine. The server count above comes from the last full run, and the UI count adds the two tests I wrote after it. I'll report the audit and test results when they finish.

**Claude:**

Yes, your local Docker is up to date. I checked that `api` and `worker` are running the new saga code and that the web bundle has the new cards. **Reload your tab and click New chat before testing.**

The integration tests are still finishing, and a `make up` runs right after them. No app code has changed since the last build, so it shouldn't change anything, but the app could blip for a moment.

The UI runs as `demo-user`, who has an upcoming AC servicing booking, so you can start straight away. Try these in order, because the last one cancels that booking:

| Say | What should happen |
|---|---|
| `Move my AC servicing to next week` | It asks which day and time, and shows no card |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 10am` | A "Move this booking?" card shows the current and new times |
| `keep it` | The booking stays as it is |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 12 noon`, then `yes` | Conflict: "your booking did not move", and it stays where it was |
| `Move my AC servicing to 14 Nov at 10am`, then Confirm | "Moved and verified", with both times |
| `Cancel my AC servicing` | A "Cancel this booking?" card appears |
| `book it` | Ignored as an answer, and the card stays open |
| `cancel it` | "Cancelled and verified" |

**What you may run into:**
- **Provider not working that hour:** the provider doesn't work about a quarter of its hours, and I can't check this before the card. Only after you confirm will you see "does not work at…", and your booking stays put. This can hit either the 10am or the noon move, so just try another hour. If noon gets this message, you've seen the failure path but not the conflict.
- **Other slots:** after a conflict, it only suggests other slots if a search in that chat listed them. Otherwise it asks you for another time.

To test on a booking you just made, use the normal flow: search, book, then say `Cancel my plumber booking`.

| Job | What it runs |
|---|---|
| **Server** | Lint, format, types, import rules and all unit tests |
| **Web** | Types, tests and build |
| **Integration** | `make test-integration`, with real PostgreSQL, Redis and workers in Compose |

- **Workflow file:** it passes `actionlint`.
- **Clean-copy run:** I ran the server and web steps on a copy of the repo with no keys or local settings. That caught a real problem: 6 tests in `test_model_retry.py` only passed here because your machine has a real `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. That key was also being sent to the local fake model server in those tests, though it never left your machine.
- **The fix:** those tests now use a fake key. I reran those 6 in the clean environment and they pass, but I didn't repeat the whole server step.
- **Integration job:** it has only run here through `make test-integration`, not on a clean copy.
- **Minutes:** the repo is private, so each run uses your GitHub Actions minutes.

**Claude:**

Your run wasn't stuck in our code. Gemini has become very slow, so the app was waiting on it.

| Time (UTC) | Average model call | Slowest call |

| **09:50** | 1.2 s | 2.1 s |
