- **The cause is outside the app:** I sent Gemini a tiny "Say ok." request directly, skipping our agent and prompt. Both tries timed out after about 45 seconds with `504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`.
- **Why it looked frozen:** "show all my bookings" needs two model calls, so it took about 45 seconds with nothing but "Thinking…" on screen. An earlier try failed after about a minute of 504s, and it reported "The AI model is not responding right now".
- **Your chat is still working:** the next messages came back, with one taking about a minute. The newest run started at 10:06:36 and was still waiting when I checked at 10:07:34. If that one hasn't answered yet, it's the same slowness. The run limit is 120 seconds, and after that you get a clear message.
- **Replies lost to reloads:** the web logs show two requests where the browser gave up before the reply arrived (status 499), most likely from a reload or New chat. So wait for a reply if you can. Those runs keep going on the server, and you just won't see their replies.

I didn't change anything. The slowness started around the same time as my last rebuild, but the rebuild only changed one line in the date code, and the direct test skipped the app anyway. I can't tell how long Gemini will stay slow. For now, you can retest later or expect slow replies.

**Claude:**

No, this doesn't look like rate limiting. A rate limit would show up as a `429` error, and we aren't getting any. What we're seeing is slow replies and `504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` timeouts, which means Gemini accepted the request but didn't finish in time.

- **No 429s in the logs:** a search of the last 15–20 minutes of API logs found no `429` or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors. The lines that matched were just timestamps and code line numbers containing "429".
- **No rate-limit events in the traces:** the app records `model_rate_limited` when Gemini refuses a call for this reason, and there are none in the last 3 hours.
- **Well under the limit:** our busiest recent minute was 7 model calls, against the free tier's 15 requests a minute.
- **Still slow:** a tiny "Say ok." call just now succeeded but took 29.7 seconds, compared with the usual 1–2 seconds for our full calls. A refused call fails right away, so this doesn't look like a refusal.

**What I can't rule out:** Google could be slowing free-tier traffic without sending an error, and that would look the same from here. Either way, it's on Gemini's side and our call volume doesn't seem to be the cause. Waiting is the simplest fix.

a card built from the provider's own booking data. Only a click or the

  a time the user never said.
- CI: server checks, web checks and integration tests on every pull request.
EOF

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:** FastAPI, PostgreSQL 17 (`errand`, `adk_sessions`, `mock_provider`, plus `*_test`; DB user `errand`), Redis 8, Google ADK 2.13.0 (thin), Gemini `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (free tier 15 requests/min), React + Vite + TS served by nginx, Docker Compose (`make up`), Alembic, taskiq + `RedisStreamBroker`. GitHub repo private `AviroopPaul/orange-assignment`.
   - **Layout:** domain-led with standard FastAPI files; shared code in `app/core/`. Routers have no DB access, services own transactions, repositories only flush, no transaction across network calls, fakes only at infra boundaries. 7 import contracts.
   - **Core rule:** model can only read and propose. Only deterministic code changes a booking, after an approval the model cannot produce.
   - **Approval path (book, cancel, reschedule):** `propose_*` writes an approval row with a SHA-256 hash; card comes from the row only; yes/no read from raw whole message (`read_decision(message, action)`) or a click, before the model runs; confirm is one transaction (conditional consume, workflow → EXECUTING, attempt row with key `<action>:<approval_id>`, outbox job `bookings.run_attempt`); publish after `finish_run`.
   - **Saga:** claims attempt with lease and `claims` fence, commits call count before each call. `book` verified only by `get_booking_status`; `cancel`/`reschedule` verified only by `list_bookings`, because `get_booking_status` knows only `book`. Token built from what the saga sees now (`token_for`, `change_token_for`); verifier refuses any difference; a refused call was never sent, and the count is put back.
   - **Dates now:** the model never works out a date. `resolve_dates` reads the user's own words (grounded check against `workflow.user_text`) and saves with no question. The next reply must show exact dd/mm/yyyy, or code prepends `Dates: <label>.`. The agent asks only if no date was given or the words can't be read, in its own words.
   - **PostgreSQL is truth, Redis only carries work.** Only `api` writes ADK sessions; workers write `errand`; model reads booking news through `prompt_note`. UI polls `/notifications` every 2 s while a booking runs.
   - **Testing practice:** unit (real mock via ASGI, real ADK loop with `ScriptedLlm`, SQLite, fakeredis), integration in Compose (`make test-integration`), `make check`, live Gemini scripts, headless Chromium, GitHub CI.

**Claude:**

Memory stores facts about the user, and the ContextAssembler decides what the model sees on each call. The transcript stays uncommitted.

## The problem it solves
Today ADK sends the full chat history on every model call. That causes two problems:
- **Cost grows with the chat:** a single correction turn after two searches already used 12,821 input tokens across 3 calls.
- **Forgetting can't work:** ADK's history is append-only. If you say "forget my address", the memory row can be removed, but the address is still in the old messages the model receives.

## What the ContextAssembler is
It's one piece of code that runs in `before_model_callback`, just before every model call. It throws away what ADK prepared and builds the request itself. That includes calls in the middle of a run, such as after a tool returns.

The assembler builds each request in five steps:
1. **Gather:** it collects the pieces listed in the table below.
2. **Filter:** SQL keeps only memories that are active, not superseded, and either explicit or confirmed by the user. An unconfirmed fact never reaches the ranking step.
3. **Rank:** a fixed score on service and scope puts the relevant memories first. For an AC request, "my AC is a Daikin" beats "I prefer a female plumber". There are no embeddings, so evals give the same result offline.
4. **Trim:** it cuts down to 8,000 estimated tokens, using a cautious chars / 3 estimate.
5. **Log:** it writes the full request and the token count per piece to `context_log` before the call. If that write fails, the model call doesn't run.

| Piece | Source | When over budget |
|---|---|---|
| System prompt and tool declarations | Code | Always kept, and counted |
| Workflow state and booking news | `errand` database | Kept |
| Current request and current tool calls | This run | Kept, but large tool results shrink first |
| Older turns | `turn_view` | Cut first |
| Summary of the older chat | Stored summary | Cut second |
| Memories | `memories` table | Cut last, lowest rank first |

## How it connects to memory
- **`turn_view`:** this is our own copy of the chat, which we can edit. The assembler reads this, not ADK's log.
- **Forgetting:** this marks the memory as forgotten, removes the text from `turn_view`, rebuilds the summary and deletes the old ADK session. Without the assembler, none of this would keep the fact from the model.
- **Worker news:** the worker can't write to ADK sessions, so a proactive cancellation notice enters through the assembler on the next turn.
- **Trimming is safe for the errand:** the area, budget and dates live on the workflow row, so cutting old chat doesn't lose them. The assembler takes over the small version of this that `instruction()` does today in [runtime.py:44](server/app/domains/agent/runtime.py:44).

## What it doesn't do
It adds no booking safety. The approval and saga rules stay exactly as they are, and it only controls what the model knows.

## How we prove it
- **E26:** 60 memories and a long chat stay within budget on every call, and only relevant facts are sent.
- **E22 and I4:** seeded marker strings are searched for in every logged context. A forgotten, superseded or unconfirmed one must never appear.
- **I5:** every logged context is within the budget.

## One gap to settle
The blueprint needs a summary and says to rebuild it on forget, but it doesn't say who writes it.
- **Code-built (my pick):** this means a short summary made from structured facts such as past errands and outcomes. It's repeatable offline, costs no model call, and can't bring back forgotten text unless that text is in the source rows.
- **Model-written:** this would read better, but it uses free-tier calls and makes evals less repeatable. It could also carry forgotten text forward in reworded form, which a marker search might miss.

# Errand Agent server: the map

Domain-led FastAPI. Each domain uses the standard files it needs, and nothing more.

```
app/
  main.py         api process (create_app, lifespan, error handlers)
  worker.py       worker process (taskiq broker and startup)
  scheduler.py    scheduler process, one copy only
  migrate.py      one-shot job: Alembic upgrade, then ADK tables
  healthcheck.py  Compose health check for worker and scheduler
  container.py    composition root (constructor injection)
  web.py          FastAPI dependencies
  core/           config, clock, database, turn lock, heartbeats
  domains/
    chat/         turn controller: limits, lock, outcomes, replies
    agent/        ADK adapter, Gemini config, scripted model, prompt, callbacks, model tools
    gateway/      the only path to any tool: rights, schema, budget, retries, sanitize, trace
    jobs/         outbox, publish, sweep, lease, taskiq broker and tasks
    workflow/     state machine, the errand's details, hard limits on search results
    bookings/     approvals, the approval hash, reading a yes or no, and the booking saga
    notifications/ what the system tells a user outside a chat turn
    tracing/      runs, trace events, cost
    system/       health, status, ping job
```

Domain files: `router.py` (HTTP only), `schemas.py` (Pydantic), `models.py` (SQLAlchemy),
`repository.py` (queries), `service.py` (business logic).

cat > core/redaction.py <<'EOF'
"""Removes a fact's text from anything we stored. Forgetting must reach every copy."""

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any

REMOVED = "[removed]"


def compile_patterns(values: Iterable[str]) -> re.Pattern[str] | None:
    """Longest first, so a whole phrase goes before a part of it. Whole words only."""
    parts = sorted({value.strip() for value in values if value.strip()}, key=len, reverse=True)
    if not parts:
        return None
    escaped = (r"\s+".join(re.escape(word) for word in part.split()) for part in parts)
    return re.compile(rf"(?<!\w)(?:{'|'.join(escaped)})(?!\w)", re.IGNORECASE)


def scrub_text(text: str, pattern: re.Pattern[str] | None) -> str:
    return pattern.sub(REMOVED, text) if pattern else text


def scrub_value(value: Any, pattern: re.Pattern[str] | None) -> Any:
    """Every string inside a JSON-like value. Keys and other types stay as they are."""
    if pattern is None:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return pattern.sub(REMOVED, value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: scrub_value(item, pattern) for key, item in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [scrub_value(item, pattern) for item in value]
    return value
EOF

import { vi } from "vitest";

/** The only fake in UI tests: the HTTP boundary. Everything above it is the real app. */
type Handler = (body: unknown) => { status?: number; json: unknown } | Promise<never>;

export function fakeApi(routes: Record<string, Handler>) {
  const calls: { key: string; body: unknown }[] = [];
  const fetchMock = vi.fn(async (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const key = `${init?.method ?? "GET"} ${String(input)}`;
    const body = init?.body ? JSON.parse(String(init.body)) : undefined;
    calls.push({ key, body });
    const handler = routes[key];
    if (!handler) {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ detail: "not found" }), { status: 404 });
    }
    const result = await handler(body);
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(result.json), { status: result.status ?? 200 });
  });
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", fetchMock);
  return calls;
}

**Claude:**

Memory and the ContextAssembler are built and running on your local stack at `http://localhost:3000`. Nothing is committed: the work is on branch `memory-context`, and the refreshed transcript is still uncommitted too.

## What you can try
- **Save a fact:** say "I live in Indiranagar, remember that." It appears on the new Memory panel, and a new chat uses it without asking.
- **Correct or forget a fact:** do it in chat or on the panel, and the old value stops reaching the model.
- **See the seeded data:** open `http://localhost:3000/?user=seed-user` to see 40 trusted facts and 8 unconfirmed ones.
- **See what was sent:** each model call now shows a "Context built" row in the trace.

## What the live Gemini run showed
- **Full flow:** it saved a fact, used it in a new chat, corrected it, then forgot it.
- **Forgetting:** afterwards neither area name was in `turn_view`, `context_log`, the errand, runs, trace events or ADK rows.
- **Budget:** the seeded user (60 memories, 240 chat messages) used an estimated 7,979 and 7,991 of 8,000 tokens. Gemini's real counts were 6,240 and 6,647.
- **Filtering:** unconfirmed, superseded and forgotten markers appeared in no logged context.

## Testing
- **What ran:**
    - the server unit test files this change touches, including the new `test_memory.py`
    - 43 UI tests
    - lint, types and import rules
    - `alembic check` on Postgres, which found no drift from the models
    - a headless Chromium layout check at three widths
- **What didn't run:** the full suite and integration tests, as you asked. CI runs them on the PR, so a failure could still show up there.
- **No integration test yet:** this feature has none of its own, so on Postgres it has only the live run and `alembic check` behind it.
- **Deliberate-break audit:** still on hold, so these tests haven't been proven to catch a break.

## Limits you may notice
- **Asking "what do you remember?" sends every trusted fact:** that includes facts about other services, for that turn. This happened in the seeded live run. It's the one known exception to "only relevant facts", so tell me if you'd rather have it ranked too.
- **Forgetting matches exact text:** if the model reworded a fact, such as "Indira Nagar" for "Indiranagar", the reworded copy stays in the stored chat.
- **Duplicate keys:** the model chooses each fact's key, so one fact could end up under two keys. Both would show on the panel.
- **Past bookings:** "same as last time" still relies on the prompt, so F8 stays Partial and E20 is not started.

## Build log
- **Status:** functional requirements are now 12 done, 1 partial and 1 not started. Non-functional are 11 done and 9 partial.
- **Blueprint changes:** I logged them, including that the summary is now built by code on each read and is not stored.
- **Bugs:** I added one to `BUGS.md`: a typed yes or no never reached the model's history. It has a regression test.
- **CI note:** the out-of-date note is fixed.

Proactive cancellation, SSE and JSONL traces are next, when you say.

**You:**

And decides to save it, maybe you could also in the chat ask in the chat window itself, whatever be the UI, second thing is after I asked it to save it, it only saved the work schedule and not my location. So these are two things that I just noticed even before testing anything.

**Claude:**

You're right on both. The second one is a real bug, and I can see why in your trace.

- **Why it wasn't trusted:** the model wrote "goes to office" but you wrote "go to office". My check needs every word of the value in your sentence, so one word's ending marked it unconfirmed.
- **Why the location was missed:** the model made only one save call, for the schedule. The prompt doesn't tell it to save each fact separately.

I'll fix both and add the automatic save with a question in chat. First I'm reading the chat UI code.

**Claude:**

Both issues are fixed and running on your local stack. Your exact message now saves both facts without you saying "remember", and with no question.

## What changed
- **Automatic saving:** the agent now watches every message for lasting facts and saves them straight away. If a message only gives facts, it saves them and then asks what you need.
- **One save per fact:** "I live in Indiranagar and go to office..." now makes two saves, one for `area` and one for `work_schedule`.
- **Word endings:** "goes to office" now counts as your statement, as we discussed.
- **Shown in the chat:** a saved fact appears under the reply as "Remembered area: Indiranagar".
- **Asked in the chat:** if your words don't clearly state a fact, a "Remember this?" card appears with Remember and Don't remember buttons. You can also type "yes", "remember that" or "no".

## Live Gemini results

| Message | What happened |
|---|---|
| Your exact message | Saved both facts, no question |
| "I prefer Hindi speaking technicians and nothing before 10 am" | Saved the language. Asked about the time, because the model wrote "not before 10 am" |
| A fact plus a request for an electrician | Saved the fact, and the search still ran |
| "Plumber in Koramangala tomorrow, budget 1000" | Saved nothing, which is right for a one-off errand |
| A fact, then "remember that" | Saved it once, and the agent said it already had it |

## Rules I chose
- **Save first, ask only when unsure:** a fact you clearly stated is saved without asking, because the "Remembered" line shows it and you can correct or forget it. Tell me if you'd rather be asked every time.
- **A question lasts one message:** if you move on, the card closes and the fact waits on the Memory panel. A later "yes" to something else can't confirm it.
- **Booking cards come first:** if a booking card is open, "yes" answers that card.

## Another bug I found
Saying no to a guess would also have forgotten the real fact under the same key. It now drops only the guess. This and your report are in `BUGS.md` with regression tests.

## Limits
- **Spotting a fact is still the model's judgement:** only the prompt asks for it, so it can miss a fact or save a one-off detail. Five live chats don't show how often that happens.
- **The check matches words, not meaning:** "I don't like Rahul" could pass as "likes Rahul". You would see it in the chat and could correct it.
- **More Gemini calls:** a turn that saves a fact usually needs one extra model call, which counts against the free-tier limit of 15 a minute.
- **Old row on your panel:** your `work_schedule` row from the earlier test is still there as unconfirmed. Click Confirm, Correct or Forget to clear it.

## Testing
I ran `test_memory.py`, `test_booking_chat.py`, `test_http_api.py`, `test_chat_service.py` and 45 UI tests, plus lint, types, import rules and `alembic check`. The full suite and integration tests still haven't run, so CI will be their first run. Nothing is committed: this is on `memory-context`, and the transcript stays uncommitted too.

**Claude:**

The date problem is fixed: replaying your exact chat on live Gemini now gets to a real date and a search. It's running on your local stack.

## Why it kept asking
The model wasn't the main problem. My date code refused its answers each time:

| You said | The model sent | What went wrong |
|---|---|---|
| "next week sometime" | "next week sometime" | The reader didn't know "sometime" |
| "lets do thur" | "Thursday next week" | This was correct, but you wrote "thur", and my check compares whole words, so "Thursday" counted as something you never said |
| "cant you find out the date?" | "Thursday next week" | Same refusal |

Each refusal told the model to ask you for a date, so it kept asking.

## What I fixed
- **Short words:** "thur" and "Thursday", "nov" and "November", "14th" and "14", and "tmrw" and "tomorrow" now count as the same word.
- **Loose words:** "sometime", "anytime" and "whenever" are ignored next to a real date. On its own, "sometime" still gets a question.
- **Narrowing a range:** after "next week", a bare "thur" now means next week's Thursday. The first replay gave this Thursday (05/11), because the model dropped "next week" again, so this rule is in code, not the prompt. "This Thursday" still means this Thursday.
- **No more asking for a calendar date:** the refusals and the prompt now say the tool works the date out.
- **A related bug:** "Tuesday or Thursday next week" used to start from this Tuesday. The week now applies to both days.

## The replay

| You said | Result |
|---|---|
| "next week sometime" | 09/11/2026 to 15/11/2026, and it searched |
| "anyday im not working" | It used your saved schedule and suggested Tuesday, Thursday or the weekend |

**Claude:**

**Your tool results were correct. The model made up the Tuesday slots, and my code set it up to do that.** No wrong booking was possible: code refused all three attempts, and no card ever appeared. I haven't changed any code yet.

## What the provider really has

I queried the mock provider directly, and it matches what we stored from the search.

| Provider | Total slots next week | Tuesday 10/11 |
|---|---|---|
| Quick AC Care | 34 | **None** |
| Trusted AC Care | 34 | 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 |
| City AC Care | 36 | 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 |

## What the model said, turn by turn

| You said | Tool call | Model said | True? |
|---|---|---|---|
| "lets go with quick" | `get_provider`, which has no slots | Monday 10:00 or 11:00 | Yes |
| "what do you suggest" | None | Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 | **No, made up** |
| "lets do tue" | `propose_booking` Tue 10:00, **refused** | No Tuesday slots | Yes, it had this right |
| "you just said..." | None | Apologised, then listed six Tuesday slots, and said "you work on Tuesdays" | **No, on both.** Your schedule is saved as Mon, Wed, Fri |
| "lets do 12" | `propose_booking` Tue 12:00, **refused** | Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 | **No, made up** |
| "lets do 11?" | `propose_booking` Tue 11:00, **refused** | Tuesday 10:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00 | **No, made up** |

## Why it happened

1. **The model can't see most of the slots (my code).** The search result shows only the first 6 of 34 slots, and later turns show the first 8 plus "(26 more)". For Quick AC Care that means Monday and part of Wednesday. No tool can read the rest, so it couldn't answer a question about Tuesday. The 6-slot cap is older, but my new assembler kept the same kind of cut, with 8.
2. **It probably mixed up providers.** The made-up times match the other two providers' Tuesday slots, which sit on the lines right next to Quick's in what it was sent. This part is my inference from the context logs, because a log can't prove why the model chose them.
3. **A refusal gives no alternatives (my code).** It only says "Choose a listed slot", without saying which slots are open. The model then invented a list, three times.
4. **The prompt encourages it (my code).** It says "list a few open slots", but nothing says to state only slots listed for that exact provider, or what to do when you push back. So when you did, it gave in and brought the made-up slots back.
5. **Nothing checks the reply.** Code checks what the model does, and checks claims that something was booked, but not what it says about availability.
6. **The model works out weekdays itself.** Slots arrive as `2026-11-10T10:00:00+05:30` with no day name. It got them right here, but that breaks our rule that the model never works out dates.

## What I ruled out
- **Memory and the assembler's trimming:** the full chat was sent, and the saved schedule was correct.
- **Tool failures:** the search returned correct data, and code refused correctly.
- **The trace panel:** the trace stores a shortened copy of each result (11 slots here), so it doesn't show what the model received. The audit used `context_log`, which does.

## Proposed fixes
1. **Send all open slots, per provider and grouped by day, with weekdays written by code.** For example: `2026-11-10 (Tue): 09:00, 10:00`. This goes in both the search result and the later-turn section. Very long date ranges would be capped by days, with a prompt to narrow the dates.
2. **Make refusals useful.** They would return that provider's real slots for that day, or the days it does have open.
3. **Tighten the prompt.**
    - State only slots listed for that exact provider.
    - If it isn't listed, it isn't open.
    - If you push back, re-read the list and don't just agree.
4. **Test it.** I'd add regression tests from this chat and replay it on live Gemini.

I wouldn't add a code check on the reply text. Matching free text against slots is fragile and would give false alarms. With the full list and useful refusals, the card stays the final check. These fixes make invented slots much less likely, but a model can still misread a list, so this won't get that risk to zero.

**You:**

cant the model query the provider tool with the exact day? instead of basically giving all of the slots to the model, can't it exactly query that particular provider by the date and the day and the time? Then there are tools are problematic, right? If we are not having that sort of functionality. And also initially, yes, initially to get available slots, it can, you know, query using the days. As well as the area, to figure out the names. It doesn't need to, you know, get all the slots in its token context.

**Claude:**

You're right, and that's a better design than my plan to send every slot. The real gap is the one you named: no tool can ask "what's open for this provider on this day?", so the model guessed.

One constraint: the brief fixes the provider's tools, and `search_providers` can't filter by provider. So I'll add our own tool, `get_open_slots(provider_id, day)`, which reads that provider's slots for that day from the stored search. The first search then returns only names, prices, ratings and which days are open. A booking still checks the slot live when it takes a hold. I'm building that now.

**Claude:**

Your design is built and running on your local stack, and in the live replay of your AC chat the agent didn't invent any slots. You were right that the tools were the problem.

## What changed
- **First search:** it returns only each provider's name, price, rating and open days, such as `2026-11-09 Mon`. No times.
- **New `get_open_slots(provider_id, day)`:** it returns one provider's times on one day.
- **Refused slots:** a refusal now lists the real times that day and the provider's open days, so the model has no reason to guess.
- **Prompt:** the model may not name a time unless the tool returned it for that exact provider in the same turn. If you dispute something, it must check again.

## Where this differs from what you described
- **It doesn't call the provider again:** the brief fixes the provider's tools, and `search_providers` can't filter by provider. So `get_open_slots` reads the stored results of the last search. A slot can go stale, but the hold still checks with the provider, and a taken slot gets refused.
- **No time filter:** you mentioned querying by time too. A day has at most about 7 slots, so the tool returns them all. `propose_booking` already checks the exact time.

## Same chat, live

| You said | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "lets go with quick" | Monday times, read from a cut-off list | Called the tool for Monday and listed the 6 real times |
| "what do you suggest" | Invented Tuesday 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 | Said Quick isn't open Tuesday, listed its real days |
| "lets do tue" | Tried to book, refused | Said it isn't open Tuesday, without trying |
| "you just said they had slots on tues" | Apologised and invented six slots | Apologised and stayed correct: not open Tuesday |
| "ok wed then, lets do 11" | Not reached | Called the tool, then showed a card for Wed 11/11, 11:00, ₹1,220 |

I also asked about Trusted AC Care on Tuesday. It listed all 7 real times, and "lets do 11" gave a correct card. The ₹1,220 above is the provider's held quote against a ₹1,020 list price, and the agent pointed that out.

## What still isn't right
- **It misread your schedule:** in one reply it said you have "Wednesdays and Fridays off", when your saved schedule says office on Mon, Wed and Fri. The saved fact was correct, so this is the model's reasoning, and no tool catches it. This model is the cheap lite tier, so this may keep happening.
- **An awkward reply:** one answer corrected itself mid-sentence with "(Wait, Quick AC Care is not open...)". The content ended up right, but it reads badly.
- **The rule on naming times is prompt-only:** code checks proposals and the card shows the real slot, but nothing checks the times written in a reply. One replay proves little, though a wrong time still can't get booked.
- **Tokens didn't really drop:** the search turn used 16,389 input tokens, up from 15,232 before, because the prompt and tool list grew. Search results are smaller, but the fix mainly improves accuracy. It doesn't save tokens yet.

## Testing
I ran the affected unit test files, plus lint, types and import rules. I also changed `test_booking_saga.py`, an integration test, so CI will be its first run, along with the full suite. Nothing is committed: this is on `memory-context`, and the transcript stays uncommitted too. It's logged as bug 14 in `BUGS.md`.

Brief: `Orange_Engineering_Assignment.pdf` in repo root (git-ignored). 2. Key Technical Concepts:

Step 1: for `watched_users()` (attempts booked/rescheduled with booking_id), `list_bookings` with `Caller.BACKGROUND`; `policy.decide(booking, on_record, already_recorded, change_running)` → `Decision(reason, notify, record)`; reasons enum `Reason`: provider_cancelled, past_booking, duplicate, not_our_booking, change_in_progress, no_change, replacements_offered, no_replacement_fits, no_preferences, dates_passed, search_failed, errand_in_progress. Repeats increment `repeats_seen`. Past booking: row status `ignored`, reason, no notice. Step 2 (`_offer_replacements`, rows in `detected`, also resumes after crash): `replacement_search(request, today)` (saved request only, start clipped to today), search via gateway, exclude cancelling provider, `apply_hard_limits`/`build_shortlist`, `best_options` top 3 by rating then price; `_close` takes turn lock with `wait_s=0` (retries next poll), `WorkflowService.reopen_in` (blank INTAKE errand closes to DONE, new legal move; DONE→DISRUPTED→COMPARING with new shortlist; another real errand → None → reason errand_in_progress); notice `replacement_options`; trace event `replacement_decision` with holds_placed 0; `settle_run(recorder,"needs_input",text,"proactive")`. """One tiny call per model. Prints status and quota details only, never the key."""

import json
import os
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

MODELS = ["gemini-2.5-flash", "gemini-3.5-flash-lite", "gemini-3-flash-preview"]
BODY = json.dumps({"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Say ok."}]}]}).encode()

for model in MODELS:
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent",
        data=BODY,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "x-goog-api-key": os.environ["GOOGLE_API_KEY"]},
    )
    started = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=40) as response:
            print(model, response.status, f"{time.time() - started:.1f}s", "ok")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        details = json.loads(error.read()).get("error", {})
        print(model, error.code, f"{time.time() - started:.1f}s", details.get("status"))
        for item in details.get("details", []):
            for violation in item.get("violations", []):
                print("  quota:", violation.get("quotaId"), violation.get("quotaValue"), violation.get("quotaDimensions"))
            if "retryDelay" in item:
                print("  retry after:", item["retryDelay"])
    except Exception as error:  # a timeout is an answer too
        print(model, "failed", type(error).__name__, f"{time.time() - started:.1f}s")
```

Yes, you've hit the daily limit, but only for `gemini-2.5-flash`. Other models on the same key still work.

- **Direct call just now:** `gemini-2.5-flash` returned 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` in 0.4 s.

- **Reset:** the retry delay is 56,954 s, so about 08:00 UTC, or 13:30 IST tomorrow.

**The limit is the real problem**
- **20 requests a day, per model:** a chat turn makes about 2.1 model calls on average, so that is only about 10 turns a day.
- **My miss:** I told you I hadn't checked this model's free-tier limits when we switched. One live run used about half of the 20, and your UI testing likely used the rest.

"""Estimated model cost, from Google's Standard tier prices checked on 2 Nov 2026."""

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Price:
    input_per_million_usd: float
    output_per_million_usd: float


PRICES: dict[str, Price] = {
    "gemini-3.5-flash-lite": Price(0.30, 2.50),
    "gemini-2.5-flash": Price(0.30, 2.50),
}


def estimate_cost_usd(model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float | None:
    """Output includes thinking tokens, as Google bills them. None means no known price."""
    price = PRICES.get(model)
    if price is None:
        return None
    return (
        input_tokens * price.input_per_million_usd + output_tokens * price.output_per_million_usd
    ) / 1_000_000
```

PRs are squash merged.

   - **Quota facts:** Gemini free tier quota `GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier`; `gemini-2.5-flash` = 20 requests a day per model, about 10 turns (avg 2.1 model calls per turn, avg 3,466 input tokens per call, avg turn 7,348 tokens, p95 16,237, max 25,710). Resets around 08:00 UTC / 13:30 IST. Limit is per model, so other models still answer. Daily limit of `gemini-3-flash-preview` is **unknown**, and could also be 20. So real-model eval runs must be careful with quota: a full live script uses about 15-20 calls. A 429 with wait over 30 s becomes `ModelRateLimited` and the busy reply (works as designed).

   - **Layout:** domain-led; routers have no DB access, services own transactions, repositories only flush, no transaction across network calls, fakes only at infra boundaries. 9 import contracts in `server/.importlinter`. `app/domains/agent` includes a scripted model. Mock provider in `server/mock_provider/` reached only over HTTP; its tool contract must not change. Web `web/src/domains/` mirrors server domains; UI tests fake only the HTTP boundary.
   - **Core rule:** model only reads and proposes; only deterministic code changes a booking after an approval the model cannot produce. PostgreSQL is truth, Redis only carries work. Only `api` writes ADK sessions under the turn lock; workers write `errand`. Every tool call goes through `ToolGateway.call`. Success text is a template after source-of-truth verification.
   - **Proactive (`domains/proactive/`):** scheduler `jobs.provider_poll` every 20 s; `policy.decide` returns `Decision(reason, notify, record)`; one unique `booking_disruptions` row per booking; notices `provider_cancelled` and `replacement_options`; no hold ever; rebooking via normal card; background work takes turn lock with `wait_s=0`.
   - **SSE:** `GET /events?user_id=&after=` with `Last-Event-ID`, Redis wake-ups carry no news, `LOOK_AGAIN_S=10`.
   - **JSONL:** `domains/tracing/jsonl.py` `JsonlTraceFiles`; `TRACE_DIR=/srv/artifacts/traces`, one file per run, first line `run_started` seq 0; bind mount `./artifacts:/srv/artifacts`.
   - **DB trace table:** `trace_events` columns: `id run_id seq kind name data latency_ms input_tokens output_tokens estimated_cost_usd created_at` (kinds include `model_call`, `model_error`, `model_rate_limited`, `model_unavailable`, `provider_cancel_detected`, `replacement_decision`). `runs` has `user_id`, `started_at`. Other tables: `workflows`, `approvals`, `booking_attempts`, `booking_disruptions`, `notifications`.
   - **Eval-relevant tooling:** `MOCK_EVAL_MODE=true make up` enables mock admin endpoints: `POST /admin/scenario` (e.g. `{"book_outcomes": ["success"]}`), `POST /admin/provider-cancel` (`{"booking_id": ...}`); mock tools at `POST /tools/list_bookings` with `X-User-Id` header. API: `POST /chat` (`user_id`, `message`, optional `session_id`) returns `run_id, session_id, outcome, reason, retry_after_s, reply, approval, memory`; `POST /approvals/{id}/confirm` with `{"user_id":...}`.
   - **Testing practice:** run only relevant tests; GitHub CI runs the full suite (`./scripts/check.sh`, `make test-integration`). Deliberate-break audits held until the whole build is ready. No Prettier config: use `--print-width 100`.

**Claude:**

# Eval approach

**Goal:** run 37 scenarios end to end with `make evals`, with no network access. After each scenario, a checker reads the databases and tests the invariants. The run writes the table itself, and reply wording is not what passes or fails a scenario.

## What is real
- **Real:** PostgreSQL, Redis, the mock provider over HTTP, worker and scheduler processes, the ADK loop, the gateway and the saga.
- **Model:** scripted in most scenarios, and recorded Gemini replies in E01, E02 and E06.
- **API:** the real app and routes, run in process so each scenario can set its own model. E37 runs it as a real process instead.
- **Network:** a separate `evals` Compose profile with its own databases, on an internal network with no internet route. The run first checks that Gemini can't be reached, and it fails if it can.

## How a scenario works
- **Simulated user:** a short script of messages and card clicks that reacts to what comes back, such as the current card ID.
- **Isolation:** scenarios run one at a time, each with a new user ID and a reset mock.
- **Time limit:** each scenario has one, so a hang becomes a failed row.
- **Scripted model change:** a step can read the last tool result, because slot IDs are only known at run time.

## How failures are forced

| Failure | Method |
|---|---|
| Booking outcomes, price or slot changes | Existing `/admin/scenario` |
| Expired hold | Existing `/admin/clock/advance` |
| Worker killed (E15, E16, E36) | `SIGKILL` on the real process while the mock hangs |
| Redis wiped | `FLUSHALL` |
| Redis or PostgreSQL down | Small TCP proxy that the harness switches off |
| Model errors and loops | Scripted steps |

E15 needs one new mock admin control, to hang the provider read just before `book`. The tool contract doesn't change, and the app gets no crash hooks.

## Invariants
These run after every scenario:
- **I1:** each booking, cancel or reschedule at the provider has one consumed approval, and its hash is recomputed.
- **I2:** at most one booking per key, and per user, provider and slot.
- **I3:** each success message has a verified attempt before it.
- **I4:** the scenario's forbidden values appear in no `context_log` row.
- **I5:** each logged context is within the token budget.
- **I6:** each run has an unbroken trace, one outcome and a reply.
- **I7:** no provider review text appears on an approval card.
- **I8:** no job or attempt is left open once the system settles.

**Checker tests:** a checker that never fails proves nothing. Each invariant gets a test that plants a violation and confirms the checker catches it.

## The table
- **Files:** `evals/results.md` and `evals/results.json`.
- **Columns:** the brief's scenario, expected, actual, pass/fail and notes, plus model type and brief category.
- **Actual:** measured from the data, for example `book calls=1, bookings=1, attempt=verified`.
- **Complete rows:** a scenario that crashes gets an ERROR row, so no scenario can go missing. Any failure makes the run exit non-zero.
- **Brief coverage:** the run fails if a category from the brief has no scenario.

## New code for E20 and F8
- **Past bookings:** code reads "same electrician as last time" from the user's words and `list_bookings`, not the model.
- **Matches:** one provider is used directly, several means the agent asks, and none means it says so.
- **Time limit:** "not before 10" uses the existing `earliest_time` filter.

## Added scenario: E37
**API killed mid-turn:** the build log lists `api` kill tests as still missing for N8, but the blueprint has no scenario for them. E37 checks that the next message works and that no booking is lost or doubled.

## Limits
- **Model judgement:** scripted runs test our code's rules, not Gemini's judgement. Recordings only show what Gemini did once.
- **I3:** a model reply is checked by its wording, so a success claim in unusual words could pass. The table will say so.
- **Quota:** I estimate recording takes about 20 calls, and this model's daily limit is still unknown. Each scenario saves its own recording, so a limit only delays the rest to the next day.

## Build order
1. **First slice:** E20 and F8, then the harness and all 8 invariants with their checker tests, proven on E01 and E11. I'll show you this first.
2. **Rest of the scenarios:** added in batches of booking failures, restarts and outages, memory and context, then proactive and limits.
3. **Bugs found on the way:** real ones go in `BUGS.md` and get fixed. I won't loosen a check to make a scenario pass.
4. **Recordings:** done last, once you've chosen the model.
5. **Finish:** add it to GitHub CI, then update the build log and README.

## Choices I've made
Tell me if you want any of these changed:
- **Recordings:** they wait for your verdict on `gemini-3-flash-preview`, and nothing before that step depends on it.
- **Branch:** I'll build on a new `eval-harness` branch cut from the current one, so the uncommitted model switch comes along.
- **Results file:** I'll commit the final `evals/results.md` as the deliverable, and CI will also save each run's copy.

**You:**

Okay, so Gemini 3 flash preview is working decently as of now. So you can, you know, make a PR and merge that. And after that, let's continue with the eval, the approach looks good. Yeah, just make sure you follow the things written in the build log as well as the blueprint that we had, the artifact at the beginning. All of the requirements over there have been met. And maybe if any requirement was newly introduced by us, that should also be met. And I would also like a CSV along with the JSON and the MD. In terms of the output result of the eval.

N2 Clear result on every exit The controller wraps every run. Any exception maps to one of six outcomes. If the model is down, the reply comes from a template. E27 to E30, I6 
 N3 Approval enforced by code The gateway refuses side-effect tools without a valid token, and it accepts them only from the saga. Evals call it directly to prove the refusal. E04 E05, I1 
 N4 Material change voids approval The hash covers all approved fields, including provider, slot and price. A mismatch at call time refuses the call and invalidates the approval. Only one approval can be pending per workflow. E08 E09 
 N5 No duplicate bookings Key derives from the approval ID. A partial unique index covers active user, provider and slot. Consuming an approval is a conditional update, so only one caller wins. The mock honours the key. E14 to E16, E32, I2 
 N6 Verify after a timeout The saga must pass through VERIFYING. The state machine has no path from a timeout to a retry or DONE without a status check. E11 E12 
 N7 No false success claims Success text is a template that needs a verified row. As a second layer, after_model_callback blocks booking claims when no verified attempt exists. This layer is a heuristic. E11 E29, I3

Only the user's click or whole-message yes approves it. A worker then books, always checks the provider's status, and only then reports success. It can cancel or move a booking the same way: a card, the user's own yes, then a worker that checks the provider before it reports success. 4	after the user's approval. The model cannot choose search inputs either: it saves details with
5	`update_request`, and code builds the search from them.

16	    turn = current_turn.get()
17	    if turn is None or turn.gateway is None or turn.tool_context is None:
18	        raise RuntimeError("tool called outside a turn")
19	    return await turn.gateway.call(tool, args, turn.tool_context)

"""taskiq entrypoints. Decode, call the service, nothing else."""

import uuid

from taskiq import AsyncBroker, Context, TaskiqDepends

from app.core.heartbeats import SCHEDULER_HEARTBEAT
from app.domains.jobs.broker import PROVIDER_POLL_TASK, RUN_JOB_TASK, SWEEP_TASK


def register_tasks(
    broker: AsyncBroker, sweep_interval_s: int, provider_poll_interval_s: int = 20
) -> None:
    @broker.task(task_name=RUN_JOB_TASK)
    async def run_job(job_id: str, context: Context = TaskiqDepends()) -> None:
        await context.state.jobs.execute(uuid.UUID(job_id))

    @broker.task(task_name=SWEEP_TASK, schedule=[{"interval": sweep_interval_s}])
    async def sweep(context: Context = TaskiqDepends()) -> None:
        # The beat is written here, so it proves scheduler, Redis and worker all work together.
        await context.state.heartbeats.beat(SCHEDULER_HEARTBEAT)
        await context.state.jobs.sweep()

    @broker.task(task_name=PROVIDER_POLL_TASK, schedule=[{"interval": provider_poll_interval_s}])
    async def provider_poll(context: Context = TaskiqDepends()) -> None:
        # A lost poll needs no recovery. The next one reads the same answer from the provider.
        await context.state.provider_poll()

"""Hard limits, applied by code before the model sees any provider.

The model must not be trusted to apply a budget or a time window. It compares what is left. The
result is also kept small, because a raw search cost over 6,000 input tokens. So it names the days a
provider is open, and `get_open_slots` gives the times of one day when they are needed.
"""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from app.domains.workflow.request import field_value, parse_time


def open_days(slots: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Written by code, so the model need not work out a date or a weekday."""
    days = {datetime.fromisoformat(slot).date() for slot in slots}
    return [f"{day.isoformat()} {day:%a}" for day in sorted(days)]


def _in_window(slot: str, earliest: Any, latest: Any) -> bool:
    """The earliest time is included and the latest is not, so mornings end before 12:00."""
    try:
        starts_at = datetime.fromisoformat(slot).time()
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return (earliest is None or starts_at >= earliest) and (latest is None or starts_at < latest)


def _slots_in_window(provider: dict[str, Any], request: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    earliest = parse_time(str(field_value(request, "earliest_time") or ""))
    latest = parse_time(str(field_value(request, "latest_time") or ""))
    return [
        slot for slot in provider.get("available_slots", []) if _in_window(slot, earliest, latest)
    ]

def replacement_search(request: dict[str, Any], today: date) -> dict[str, Any] | Reason:
    """The saved request, moved on to today. There is no search without the user's own limits."""
    if missing_required(request):
        return Reason.NO_PREFERENCES
    start = date.fromisoformat(field_value(request, "start_date"))
    end = date.fromisoformat(field_value(request, "end_date"))
    if end < today:
        return Reason.DATES_PASSED
    args = search_args(request)
    args["date_range"] = {"start": max(start, today).isoformat(), "end": end.isoformat()}

**Claude:**

**No, the brief doesn't need them, and I recommend dropping them.** It says automated evals must run offline "against a scripted or recorded model", so the scripted scenarios are enough. The recordings were our own addition in the blueprint (N17). I've stopped the recording run, and it saved nothing.

**Quota**
- **Per-minute limit:** `gemini-3-flash-preview` allows 5 requests a minute on the free tier. That's about 2 chat turns a minute, so you can hit it while testing in the UI too.
- **My use:** my first attempt hit this limit, so I spent about 6 real calls plus one quota check. The second attempt may have made a few more before I stopped it, and I don't have an exact count.
- **Recovery:** a per-minute limit clears within about a minute. The daily limit is still unknown.

**If we drop them**
- **Table:** it has the 38 scripted scenarios, which is well over the brief's 20. `make evals` makes no real model calls.
- **What we lose:** no automated eval tests Gemini's own judgement, such as not re-asking a question or ignoring an injected review. Your earlier live checks and the live demo would cover that instead, and the table and build log will say so.
- **Blueprint:** I'd record this under "Changes from the blueprint", and N17 would be marked done on that basis.
- **Keeping the option:** `make evals-record` would stay as an optional command. The recorded rows would appear only if recordings exist.

**If you'd rather have them:** one recording run makes about 20 calls over about 5 minutes, spaced 13 seconds apart to stay under the per-minute limit. It could still hit the unknown daily limit, so it should run when you aren't testing.

**Where the build stands**
- **Scenarios:** the last full run passed 37 of 38. I then fixed E24, whose expectation was wrong, and reran it with E28 and E37, and all three passed. A final full run is still due.
- **Bugs found by the evals:** a cancelled tool call left a gap in the trace, and a killed API left its run open for good. Both are fixed, each with a regression test, but neither is in `BUGS.md` yet.
- **Past bookings:** "same electrician as last time" is now resolved by code, including asking when two past providers fit (E20, E20B).
- **Results files:** each run writes `evals/results.md`, `results.json` and `results.csv`.
- **Still to do:** the final full run, the CI job, the automated checks for N19 and N20, and the docs. Nothing from the eval work is committed yet.

**You:**

All right. So instead of running the whole suite again, can't we run the one sort of eval run that was missed and append it to the set of results so that we don't have to run the whole test again, because 37 of the 38 runs had passed, the test had passed, right?

**A full run costs very little:**
- **Quota:** none. These scenarios use the scripted model and have no route to the internet, so they can't rate limit you.
- **Time:** about 2 minutes of scenarios, plus a short image build and startup.
- **Why it's better than merging:** the table should come from one run of one version of the code. The harness has also changed since that full run, so the rows would come from two different versions.

**Two changes I'd make first:**
- **Partial runs:** an `--only` run will write to its own file, so this can't wipe the full table again. After that, you could rerun a single scenario without touching the main results.
- **Recorded rows:** R01, R02 and R06 will only appear if their recordings exist. There are none, so they'd stay out of the table and no real calls would be made. You haven't decided on the recordings yet, and this keeps them off until you do.

    "OpenAI-style key": re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}"),

}
# These must never travel with the repo or into an image.
MUST_IGNORE = {".gitignore": ".env", "server/.dockerignore": ".env"}


def find_secrets(text: str, known_values: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    found = [name for name, pattern in PATTERNS.items() if pattern.search(text)]
    if any(value and value in text for value in known_values):
        found.append("The value of GOOGLE_API_KEY")
    return found


def scan_tracked_files(root: Path, known_values: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
    listed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    )
    problems = []
    for name in listed.stdout.splitlines():
        path = root / name
        if Path(name).name == ".env" or Path(name).name.startswith(".env.") and "example" not in name:
            problems.append(f"{name}: an env file is tracked")
        if not path.is_file():

The eval harness is finished: **`make evals` passes 38 of 38 scenarios in one full run on the final code**, with no invariant violations. The scenarios took about 2 minutes and made no real model calls. Nothing is committed yet.

## What you have now
- **Results:** [results.md](../evals/results.md), [results.json](../evals/results.json) and [results.csv](../evals/results.csv), all written by the run. A run with `--only` now writes to `results.partial.*`, so it can't wipe the full table again.
- **Invariants:** I1 to I8 are checked from the databases after every scenario. Tests also plant violations to prove the checker can fail.
- **Added scenarios:** E20B covers two past providers that both fit, and E37 kills the real API mid-turn.
- **Past bookings (F8):** "same electrician as last time" is now resolved by code, and the agent asks if two providers fit.
- **Offline proof:** the run stops if it can reach Gemini.
- **New CI jobs:** one runs the evals. The other does a clean `make up` and a secret scan of the repo and image.

## Bugs the evals found
All three are fixed and logged in `BUGS.md`:
- **Trace gap:** when parallel tool calls ran out of budget, one lost its trace event.
- **Dead runs:** a killed API left its run open forever. The sweep now closes these.
- **Guard wording:** the false-claim guard's own reply read like a success claim, so I reworded it.

## Not done or not verified
- **CI jobs:** they haven't run yet, so N19 and N20 stay Partial until the next PR.

# Errand Agent: design note

**Core rule:** the model reads and proposes. Only deterministic code changes a booking, after an approval the model cannot produce. FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Google ADK and Gemini, run by one Compose command.

**State model.** One `workflows` row per errand: `INTAKE → SEARCHING → COMPARING → AWAITING_APPROVAL → EXECUTING → VERIFYING → DONE`, plus `DISRUPTED`, `FAILED` and `LIMIT_REACHED`. A transition table rejects illegal moves, and a row lock with a version check stops overwrites. The model has no tool that sets state. Nothing that executed reaches `DONE` without a status check. Every run ends in one of six outcomes, with a reply, inside hard limits: 8 model calls, 12 tool calls, 120 s.

**Approval enforcement.** The model has no `book`, `cancel` or `reschedule` tool. `propose_booking` takes a hold and writes an approval row with a SHA-256 hash of the action, user, provider, slot, prices, hold and expiry. The card comes from that row, never from model text or reviews. A yes is a click, or a whole-message match read from the raw message before the model runs, so "yes, but Saturday" is a change. Every tool goes through one gateway, which accepts side effects only from the saga, w

# Demo plan: 5 minutes, one story

**The story:** one customer needs a plumber. They give partial details, change their mind, read a poisoned review, book through a provider timeout, lose the booking to a provider cancel, and rebook through a price change. Then they come back for "the same electrician as last time", and forget a fact.

**The brief asks for:** one full booking, with the chat and trace side by side. A live failure is a strong plus. This plan shows three.

## The limit that shapes this plan

- **5 model calls a minute:** that is the free tier of `gemini-3-flash-preview`. A wait under 30 s happens by itself, as a pause. A longer one gives the "AI model is busy" reply.
- **Budget:** about 20 calls across the 5 minutes. No minute should go over 5, so keep to the start times below.
- **Code-only steps cost nothing:** Confirm, a typed "yes", provider events and the Memory panel make no model calls. Those are where the story has its biggest moments.
- **Call counts are estimates:** they come from about 260 real turns, where a turn took 2 to 3 calls.
